title: Elk Knob State Park: Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt
description:
Join the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Elk Knob State Park. Journey through northern hardwood forest, follow winding mountain trails, and explore the unique ecosystems of this high-elevation park. Keep your eyes open—what signs of wildlife or weather-shaped landscapes will you uncover? Look for unique rocks that make Elk Knob a very special clue in North Carolina’s geologic history. Start at the Visitor Center and scan the QR code in your Actionbound app. Flyers with the QR code will be placed in the Park Office and on all park map kiosks. 

The adventures are available on the Actionbound app – a free download to your cellphone through your phone’s app store. There’s no need to create a profile and no personal data is collected with Actionbound. You simply find new hunts by searching for the park name or scanning the associated QR code posted for your park’s adventure.

This program is made possible through a partnership with the NC Science Trail (ncsciencetrail.org)! Visit their website for more Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunts being held in other NC State Parks and for other programs being offered throughout the state. 

This scavenger hunt is running now through April 30, 2026.

title: Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt!
description: Embark on the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Lake James State Park! Located in Burke and McDowell counties 50 miles northeast of Asheville, Lake James State Park includes two areas to access this picturesque lake that are perfect for boating, swimming, and fishing. Campsites at both Catawba River and Paddy's Creek accesses provide an opportunity to spend the night by the lake, with some sites accessible only by paddling. Trails include bike trails at Paddy's Creek, the kid-friendly Holly Discovery Trail, the historic Overmountain Victory Trail, and the Fonta Flora State Trail.

title: Grandfather Mountain Scavenger Hunt
location: Boone Fork Parking Area, Milepost 299.9 on the Blue Ridge Parkway
description:
Join us all month long for NC April Science Festival with this self-guided scavenger hunt up to Flat Rock View. Park at Boone Fork Parking Area (milepost 299.9 on the Blue Ridge Parkway), find the flyer by the map at the start of the trailhead, scan the QR code in the Actionbound app, and start completing the Grandfather Mountain State Park bound! The QR code is also attached to this event if you'd like to scan earlier and see what adventure you'll be going on.

This scavenger hunt takes you up Daniel Boone Scout Trail to Flat Rock View, which is 3.6 miles round trip. The hike is moderately strenuous, and climbs 1,050 feet up to Flat Rock View. 

This is a self-guided hike, please wear appropriate hiking shoes and dress for the weather.

There are no bathrooms at Boone Fork Parking Area.

title: Visions of Freedom, Exhibit #1 (Iredell County Public Library: Main Branch-Statesville)
location: Iredell County Public Library, Main level
description:
Iredell County Public Library Commemorates 250 Years of Freedom with Year-Long Exhibit Series

The Iredell County Public Library will host a series of four local history exhibits throughout 2026 as part of America 250, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The inaugural exhibit, Visions of Freedom, will open to the public on January 12 on the Main floor of the Statesville branch library.

Visions of Freedom will focus on highlighting local landmarks, Revolutionary era residents, and important social movements that not only shaped the nation, but the Iredell County community. This free exhibit will offer a blend of information, images, and engaging interactive activities designed to appeal to visitors of all ages.

For more details about the exhibit series and upcoming local history events, please visit our website at https://iredell.lib.nc.us or contact Shellie Taylor at michelle.taylor@iredellcountync.gov

Statesville Library Hours: M-Th 8am-8pm, F & Sat 9am-6pm

title: Village of Pinehurst NCDNCR America 250 Exhibits
description:
The Village of Pinehurst will be displaying two of the NC Department of Natural & Cultural Resources exhibits throughout 2026.

"Forging a Nation" will be on display at the Cannon Park Community Center, 210 Rattlesnake Trail, Pinehurst, NC 28374.

"People of Colonial North Carolina" will be on display at Assembly Hall, 395 Magnolia Rd., Pinehurst, NC 28374.

The Given Memorial Library & Tufts Archives (150 Cherokee Road, Pinehurst, NC 28374) will also have smaller versions of the exhibits on display throughout the year and will rotate between the different exhibit subjects periodically.

title: "Making Our Voices Heard: North Carolinians Fighting for Civil Rights" Exhibit
description: This traveling exhibit tells the stories of seven everyday North Carolinians and extraordinary leaders — Gertrude Weil, Henry Owl, Joe Lewis, Abraham Galloway, Ronald Mace, James Hunter, and Willa Player — who petitioned, protested, and organized to expand democracy. The exhibit explores change, freedom, civic responsibility, and overcoming challenges by telling the story of a few North Carolinians who have raised their voices to call out injustice and fully participate in our democratic society.

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

title: The Road Through “Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell”
description:
The Road Through Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell by photographer, oral historian, and U.S. Marine Corps veteran Theresa Scott. This deeply personal documentary exhibition explores the lived experiences of LGBTQIA+ veterans who served under restrictive military policies. 
Through intimate portrait photography paired with first-person oral histories, Scott brings forward stories long silenced by institutional policy and cultural pressure. Drawing on her own service, she offers viewers an unflinching look at the realities faced by service members who were expected to serve with honor while hiding essential parts of who they were. 
Exhibition Dates: February 1 – April 26, 2026
Artist Talk & Reception: March 26, 5:30–7:00 p.m.

title: Women's Only Needle Felting: Sculpting & Painting with Wool
location: The Joel Fund, 822 S White Street, Wake Forest, 27587
description:
When: Mondays, 1:00pm – 4:00pm 
Dates: Mon: 3/9; 3/16; 3/23 
Please Note: All classes and workshops are for Military Connected Individuals who are 18 years or older. This particular class is for military-connected women over 18 years or older. 
Wool can be used as a medium to paint a landscape or a portrait or be sculpted into a 3-dimensional piece of art! This unique art has been used to illustrate children’s books and in stop-motion animation. Artists have begun to truly appreciate the practicality of using this inexpensive natural resource in ornaments, pin cushions, pillows, hanging art, and much, much more! 
In this class, students will learn the techniques to make both a flat, 2-dimensional picture and a 3-dimensional sculpture piece. Students will develop self-expression through manipulation of colors and textures of wool. 
We offer scholarships for those who cannot afford the registration fee. Email the Operation ART Program Manager at isabella@thejoelfund.org to receive the scholarship promo code with your name and email address.

title: Libraries as Spaces of Opportunity Panel
location: Witherspoon Student Center, African American Cultural Center Gallery and Library (218)
description:
Join the African American Cultural Center (AACC) for a session on how the NC State Libraries can support your academic, professional and personal growth. You will engage with authors and librarians to learn how to leverage library resources and spaces and the expertise of its staff.  You will also explore opportunities for research and creative projects and learn why representation in collections is important.

The event will offer insights for anyone interested in research, writing or lifelong learning. However, it will be particularly valuable for students majoring in English, history, journalism, sociology, anthropology, political science, psychology, arts and information science. You'll leave with practical strategies, new connections and inspiration to explore yourself and the world around you. Student attendees will have a chance to win one of two Patron Prize kits containing limited-edition AACC Library swag, a free book, library starter materials and more.

This event will close with a book signing by Zelda Lockhart and C.M. Lockhart. You can buy their books at the event or bring your own copies. The first 20 students to register for the event will receive a free book by Zelda Lockhart or C.M. Lockhart.

All are welcome to attend. The event is part of the AACC's celebration of National Library Week.

title: The Art and Science of Plant Care
description:
Caring for plants is both an art and a science — part intuition, part know-how. Every gardener, from beginner to expert, faces the same essential questions: When should I prune? How much should I water? What’s the best way to plant, fertilize or repot? In this class, Bryce Lane will bring decades of horticultural expertise to demystify these everyday tasks, showing you not just what to do but why it works.

Over eight weeks, you’ll explore the fundamental practices that keep gardens thriving, learning how to perform each one with confidence and purpose. You’ll uncover the science behind good technique — understanding how soil, water, nutrients and plant biology interact — while also developing the practical judgment that comes only with experience.

Each session will focus on one key aspect of plant care, building a complete toolkit for growing healthier, more resilient plants in any garden setting.

title: America 250 Veterans Forum
description:
Cape Fear Community College is planning a special panel discussion series as part of the nationwide celebration of America’s 250th birthday; it is looking for local veterans and military family members willing to share their stories.

CFCC is seeking participants who served , or the family members of those who served, during the following eras:

World War II

Korean War

Vietnam War

Modern conflicts, including Iraq and Afghanistan

The WWII panel discussion will take place April 6, followed by the Korean and Vietnam wars on April 7 and modern conflicts on April 8. These panels will highlight personal experiences, service, and reflections across generations, helping preserve local military history while honoring those who have served.

Interested participants can contact Director of Veteran Services Jason Bocchino at jbocchino@cfcc.edu or 910-362-7106.

title: Sexual Assault Awareness Month Denim Installation
description: Throughout April, the Women’s Center will have a Denim Day–themed installation in the Talley Student Union lobby gallery as part of Sexual Assault Awareness Month. This installation uses denim as a visual symbol of solidarity with survivors and challenges harmful myths and victim-blaming narratives. Visitors can engage with the display as an educational and reflective experience, learning about the history of Denim Day, the impact of sexual violence and ways to support survivors on campus. The installation will offer a consistent awareness-raising presence in one of the university’s most visible community spaces.

title: Spy Training 101: Decode a Secret Message
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
Pretend you’ve been recruited as a member of the Culper Spy Ring, and you need to know how to decipher a message written in invisible ink. Supplies include a paint brush, water, drying cloth, vitriol (diluted sulfuric acid), Thomas Jefferson cipher and “furnace box.” Read the clues to find the coin with a hidden message, reveal the message using the brush and vitriol, then use the cipher to decode the message.

Contact: Nancy Locquet Absillis, nancy.locquet@naturalsciences.org

title: Lake Raleigh Woods Hike
description:
Please join us on a monthly basis for a walk through the Lake Raleigh Woods, one of NC State's hidden gems and Hallowed Spaces. The hike is about 1.5 miles. Below are a few things to remember for the hike:

Make sure to park in the northwest corner of the Park Alumni Center parking lot a little before 9 a.m. for a brief safety conversation. Parking is free for everyone. Wear closed-toed shoes and bring a water bottle.Check the weather forecast and wear weather-appropriate clothing on the hike.Restrooms are available in the Alumni Center. There are no facilities on the trail.The hike will last approximately 90 minutes but could be a little shorter depending on the group's pace. Space is limited for each hike. Be sure to register.

Lake Raleigh Woods Hikes are recognized as a Campus Nature Rx Program, an international movement built around encouraging universities and their communities to engage with the physical and mental health benefits of being in nature.

title: Project Learning Tree - Together for Birds
description:
Join other K-5 classroom and nonformal educators as we explore Project Learning Tree activities focused on birds.

Together for Birds is PLT’s Newest Activity Collection!

Birds are a wonderful introduction to the natural world and happen to be just outside your door! Whether in the city or a forest, a variety of birds are usually within easy eyeshot or earshot. The activities are designed for educators to use with students in grades K-2, with variations for grades 3-5. The collection is filled with enhanced bird-specific content such as new enrichment experiences, recommended reading, forest facts, accompanying posters, and charts. Every participant will leave with a guide of this collection.

This workshop counts toward NC Environmental Education Certification (Criteria I) and consists of six contact hours that may count toward CEUs for teachers.

 

Location: Carolina Beach State Park 
Workshop Cost: $25
The PLT activity guides are provided free of charge to participants through support from the NC Forestry.
For additional workshop information, call 910-772-0546.

title: A Creek in Carolina: Artworks by Bobby C. Martin
description: A Creek in Carolina : Artworks by Bobby C. Martin will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. Nationally recognized artist Bobby C. Martin (Muscogee Creek) presents a solo exhibition tracing the pathways connecting ancestral Mvskoke homelands to Indian Territory. Drawing from family photographs and archival materials, Martin weaves encaustic, collage, maps, hymns, and personal imagery to reframe histories of forced removal as stories of resilience, survival, and continuity—inviting viewers to reflect on their own family histories and the enduring presence of Mvskoke people.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

title: Stories Told by Breath: Native American Voices in North Carolina
description:
Stories Told by Breath will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. This exhibition celebrates the creativity, memory, and cultural continuity of Native American artists connected to North Carolina. 

The exhibition brings together a rich range of media—clay, beadwork, textiles, printmaking, regalia, sculpture, and multimedia—woven with storytelling to form a vibrant experience of artistic practice in North Carolina.

Artists include Senora Lynch (Haliwa-Saponi), Karina McMillan (Lumbee), Harlen Chavis (Lumbee), Aaron Baumgardner (Catawba),Coda Cavalier (Occaneechi Band of the Saponi Nation), Amy Postoak (Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians)& Johnny Postoak (Muscogee Creek)of Three Sisters Designs, Rhiannon “Skye” Tafoya (Eastern Band of Cherokee & Santa Clara Pueblo), Joshua Adams (Eastern Band of Cherokee), Idalis Dial (Coharie), Tim Locklear (Lumbee), NC State students Ashtyn Thomas (Lumbee) and Victoria Wilson (Haliwa-Saponi), Gwen Locklear (Lumbee) and Alexandra Williams portrait photographs of Powwows at Dix Park. Together, these artists explore heritage, craft, and storytelling as a living continuum of creativity, connecting ancestral knowledge with contemporary expression.

title: The House of Ideas: Plants in Art Exhibition
location: Gregg Museum of Art & Design, Cabaniss Gallery
description: The House of Ideas: Plants in Art will be on exhibit in the Cabaniss Gallery in the Historic Chancellor’s Residence every Tuesday-Saturday until May 31, 2026. This exhibition is a participatory learning lab that uncovers the artistic representation of plants in our lives and in the natural world. It features objects from the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Collection that depict the roles of plants from nourishment and communal living to the scientific study of human health. The House of Ideas offers a relaxing room for botanical sketching and a self-guided tour of the museum’s garden.

title: Through Our Eyes, In Our Hands: Prioritizing Indigenous Knowledge in Museums
description:
Through Our Eyes, In Our Hands: Prioritizing Indigenous Knowledge in Museums will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until June 27, 2026. This exhibition foregrounds Native perspectives on the stewardship of cultural belongings and the history and future of repatriation. This exhibition transforms the museum into a site of learning, self-examination, and responsibility.

Visitors are guided through the intertwined histories of museum collecting, cultural consultation, and the journey to repatriation. Archival materials, personal accounts, and community-based narratives offer insight into the significance of the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (NAGPRA) and the ongoing work beyond its legal requirements. Rather than presenting repatriation as a transactional process, this exhibition emphasizes its cultural, spiritual, emotional, and relational dimensions—its power to restore connections and honor ancestors and communities.

title: Defending Basic Needs Programs Against Claims of Fraud
description:
Topic: Defending Basic Needs Programs Against Claims of Fraud 
Description: Citing claims of fraud, the Trump administration has made efforts to freeze or delay funding for basic needs programs. You’ve seen the news about frozen child care funding in Minnesota, and attempts to extend such a freeze to other states. Now, members of Congress are claiming fraud as they propose cuts in many other programs that serve people with low incomes. 

What do voters think about these claims? How can advocates make the strongest defense of basic needs programs? What messages are persuasive; which ones aren’t? 

Join us to learn about timely new public opinion polling from nationally known and respected Hart Research, and the messaging advice drawn from these findings. You’ll get what you need to know from Guy Molyneux, Hart Research Partner and experienced analyst, joined by others to provide the policy context and practical message tips you need. Whether you are working on local, state, or federal advocacy, these findings will help you be more effective. This webinar is sponsored by the Partnership for Basic Needs (PBN), of which CHN is a member; the Hart Research polling was commissioned by PBN.

We will explore our surroundings behind the visitor center while paying special attention to the characteristics of tree leaves all around us to help complete the “Leaf No Doubt” tree challenge! After this program, your child(ren) will be one step closer to achieving their tree field focus badge! By learning about leaves, we can make more confident tree identifications which is an important skill. Observing different tree species can tell us so much about a habitat, surrounding ecosystem, AND what wildlife species are supported by those trees. 
ecoEXPLORE is a community science program, created by the North Carolina Arboretum, where children of all ages are able to learn how to identify wildlife around them, help real scientists track wildlife activity, and earn fun badges and prizes all at the same time! title: Carolina Science Cafe: Science Under Pressure
location: Haw River Tap & Table, 300 E Main St C, Carrboro, NC, 27510, United States
description:
(Megan Mendenhall / Office of Research Communications)




Science Under Pressure: What’s at Stake for Research at Carolina



UNC-Chapel Hill generates over $1 billion in research annually with discoveries that shape medicine, technology, and public health across North Carolina and beyond. However, the federal landscape that funds this work is shifting fast. Join UNC’s Vice Chancellor for Research, Dr. Penny Gordon-Larsen, for an inside look at what Carolina scientists are building, what’s at stake in Washington, and why it matters to all of us. 



Designed for adults, Carolina Science Cafe is a free program that explores science topics making national and international headlines, offering the chance to meet the experts behind the work. This special program is hosted at Haw River Tap & Table in Carrboro on the first Tuesday of every month. Light appetizers are available for all attendees. 













About the Speaker



Penny Gordon-Larsen, PhD, Vice Chancellor for Research and William R. Kenan, Jr. Distinguished Professor in Nutrition 





(Megan Mendenhall / Office of Research Communications)




As vice chancellor for research, Gordon-Larsen develops, sets strategic direction, and provides support for UNC’s $1.5 billion research enterprise. She is responsible for research infrastructure, operations, and regulatory compliance, research development, translation, and communications, as well as strategic research partnerships. In addition, she oversees 13 pan-campus, interdisciplinary research centers and institutes. She works across campus with the University’s research deans, center/ institute directors, and key institutional leaders to strategically advance Carolina’s research enterprise. She is an obesity researcher and has served as principal investigator on research projects totaling over $23.6 million and has served as a co-investigator on an additional $49.1M interdisciplinary research team projects with collaborators. Her NIH-funded research portfolio ranges from molecular and genetic to environmental and societal-level factors that influence health and obesity and its cardiometabolic consequences.  



Gordon-Larsen served as president of The Obesity Society in 2015 and a member of the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases Advisory Council from 2020 to 2023. She also served on the 2020–2030 Strategic Plan for NIH Nutrition Research Thought Leaders Panel, the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases Strategic Plan Working Group, and the NIH Behavioral and Social Sciences Research Integration Working Group. She is on the Executive Committees for Research of the Association of American Universities and the Association of Public and Land-Grant Universities and is currently serving on the Joint Associations Group (JAG) on Indirect Costs, a coalition of national organizations representing academic, medical, and independent research institutions.

title: *IN-PERSON* SF/F Group
description:
Durham Writers Group
We will be at the People's Solidarity Hub at 1809 Chapel Hill Rd, Durham. This venue does not serve food or drink, but feel free to bring your own. There is a kitchenette for our use, but be sure to clean up afterwards. The space might be a little cozy; please consider masking or staying home if you have a respiratory ailment.

This sub-group focuses on Speculative Fiction, including Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror. If you have anything that falls under that category — be it short story, poem, novel-in-progress or screenplay — then come! We'd love to hear from you.

Our format allows each reader 15 minutes to present their work aloud, followed by approximately 20 minutes of feedback from the other attendees. To ensure fairness, each attendee is limited to 1 minute of Initial Feedback time. During that period, the author remains silent. Next, we have a 5 minute Free-For-All discussion about the work -- then the author may speak. (We usually get through three readers.)

Though not required, in order to receive more in-depth feed-back, readers may post their work in advance on our Google Group:
https://groups.google.com/d/forum/durham-sff-writers-group

We ask that participants keep their comments constructive and respectful, focusing on what works or doesn't work in the piece.

We also ask that readers provide a warning, both on the Google Group and during the meeting, if their story features content that some readers might find upsetting. This includes descriptions of violence or sexual content.

Readers are:
• Milbre
• Ryan
• Abigail

Backup Readers are:
• Baxter
• Sigma
• James

Deep Backup:
• Fabian

***

***We meet every Tuesday at the same time, but alternate between In-Person*** ***and on Zoom. Members may attend both formats, if desired, but readers will be listed separately under the In-Person or Zoom weeks.***

title: Beer and Banjos: The Holland Brothers
location: Bowstring Pizza and Brewyard, 1930 Wake Forest Rd, Raleigh, NC, 27608, United States
description:
From the Piedmont region of North Carolina, the Holland Brothers play a style of music rooted in old-school country and country blues, with close harmonies and blues harmonica. Drawing inspiration from Charlie Poole to Charlie Patton, from Muddy Waters to the Memphis Jug Band, from the country gospel sounds of Flatt and Scruggs and the Louvin Brothers, from the high lonesome sound of Bill Monroe, or from the pairing of Woody Guthrie and Cisco Houston, the brothers have appeared in publications and events such as No Depression, Our State, the North Carolina State Fair, Billboard Magazine, and the New York Times and continue to garner praise and gain new fans daily. Learn more about the Holland Brothers here. 
Beer and Banjos is a free, family-friendly evening of roots music every Tuesday at Raleigh’s Bowstring Pizza and Brewyard. Hosted by the mighty local musicians known collectively as the Beer and Banjos Allstars, these weekly concerts feature guest musicians and take place on Bowstring’s spacious patio when the weather allows, or inside by the bar when rain, heat, or cold threaten the vibe. 
Tips for the musicians are gratefully accepted (look for a helper walking around with a bucket for cash and QR codes for online tips), and don’t forget to check out the merch table. Bowstring serves tasty pizza and other food as well as cold beer and other beverages. 
Learn more about Beer and Banjos events statewide here.

title: America 250 Veterans Forum
description:
Cape Fear Community College is planning a special panel discussion series as part of the nationwide celebration of America’s 250th birthday; it is looking for local veterans and military family members willing to share their stories.

CFCC is seeking participants who served , or the family members of those who served, during the following eras:

World War II

Korean War

Vietnam War

Modern conflicts, including Iraq and Afghanistan

The WWII panel discussion will take place April 6, followed by the Korean and Vietnam wars on April 7 and modern conflicts on April 8. These panels will highlight personal experiences, service, and reflections across generations, helping preserve local military history while honoring those who have served.

Interested participants can contact Director of Veteran Services Jason Bocchino at jbocchino@cfcc.edu or 910-362-7106.

location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences

Supplies include a paint brush, water, drying cloth, vitriol (diluted sulfuric acid), Thomas Jefferson cipher and “furnace box.” Read the clues to find the coin with a hidden message, reveal the message using the brush and vitriol, then use the cipher to decode the message.

title: Elk Knob State Park: Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt
description:
Join the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Elk Knob State Park. Journey through northern hardwood forest, follow winding mountain trails, and explore the unique ecosystems of this high-elevation park. Keep your eyes open—what signs of wildlife or weather-shaped landscapes will you uncover? Look for unique rocks that make Elk Knob a very special clue in North Carolina’s geologic history. Start at the Visitor Center and scan the QR code in your Actionbound app. Flyers with the QR code will be placed in the Park Office and on all park map kiosks. 

The adventures are available on the Actionbound app – a free download to your cellphone through your phone’s app store. There’s no need to create a profile and no personal data is collected with Actionbound. You simply find new hunts by searching for the park name or scanning the associated QR code posted for your park’s adventure.

This program is made possible through a partnership with the NC Science Trail (ncsciencetrail.org)! Visit their website for more Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunts being held in other NC State Parks and for other programs being offered throughout the state. 

This scavenger hunt is running now through April 30, 2026.

title: Visions of Freedom, Exhibit #1 (Iredell County Public Library: Main Branch-Statesville)
location: Iredell County Public Library, Main level
description:
Iredell County Public Library Commemorates 250 Years of Freedom with Year-Long Exhibit Series

The Iredell County Public Library will host a series of four local history exhibits throughout 2026 as part of America 250, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The inaugural exhibit, Visions of Freedom, will open to the public on January 12 on the Main floor of the Statesville branch library.

Visions of Freedom will focus on highlighting local landmarks, Revolutionary era residents, and important social movements that not only shaped the nation, but the Iredell County community. This free exhibit will offer a blend of information, images, and engaging interactive activities designed to appeal to visitors of all ages.

For more details about the exhibit series and upcoming local history events, please visit our website at https://iredell.lib.nc.us or contact Shellie Taylor at michelle.taylor@iredellcountync.gov

Statesville Library Hours: M-Th 8am-8pm, F & Sat 9am-6pm

title: "Making Our Voices Heard: North Carolinians Fighting for Civil Rights" Exhibit
description: This traveling exhibit tells the stories of seven everyday North Carolinians and extraordinary leaders — Gertrude Weil, Henry Owl, Joe Lewis, Abraham Galloway, Ronald Mace, James Hunter, and Willa Player — who petitioned, protested, and organized to expand democracy. The exhibit explores change, freedom, civic responsibility, and overcoming challenges by telling the story of a few North Carolinians who have raised their voices to call out injustice and fully participate in our democratic society.

title: Big Tree Paddle
description:
Few people know about the "Big Tree" at Merchants Millpond, and even fewer have actually been to it. 

The "Big Tree", as many call it, is actually the second largest tree in the state of North Carolina, and we periodically lead paddles to it. Be warned: this is an all day adventure and not for the faint of heart. This paddle lasts from about 9AM-4PM but it is well worth it! Paddlers should bring appropriate clothing, plenty of water, a packed lunch, and sunscreen. A good hat is also recommended. Depending on water level of the millpond, there is always a chance paddlers will have to drag boats over beaver dams. There are a limited number of spots for this event and registration prior to the event date is required. 

Canoes are avaliable for rent at a cost of $25 per canoe. Canoes hold 2 people. 

Come out and learn about some of the things that make Merchants Millpond such an interesting place to be!

We will leave at 9:00 AM sharp. Please meet at the visitor center around 8:30 AM for orientation. 

To register, please call the visitor center at 252-357-1191

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

title: The Road Through “Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell”
description:
The Road Through Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell by photographer, oral historian, and U.S. Marine Corps veteran Theresa Scott. This deeply personal documentary exhibition explores the lived experiences of LGBTQIA+ veterans who served under restrictive military policies. 
Through intimate portrait photography paired with first-person oral histories, Scott brings forward stories long silenced by institutional policy and cultural pressure. Drawing on her own service, she offers viewers an unflinching look at the realities faced by service members who were expected to serve with honor while hiding essential parts of who they were. 
Exhibition Dates: February 1 – April 26, 2026
Artist Talk & Reception: March 26, 5:30–7:00 p.m.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

title: Women at the Edge of War: Carolina Piedmont's Heroines of the American Revolution

title: April 8 - Getting Started with FiftyOne
description:
Raleigh AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
This workshop provides a technical foundation for managing large scale computer vision datasets. You will learn to curate, visualize, and evaluate models using the [open source FiftyOne app](https://docs.voxel51.com/).

**Date, Time and Location**

Apr 8, 2026
10 AM PST - 11 AM Pacific
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/getting-started-with-fiftyone-april-8-2026)**

The session covers data ingestion, embedding visualization, and model failure analysis. You will build workflows to identify dataset bias, find annotation errors, and select informative samples for training. Attendees leave with a framework for data centric AI for research and production pipelines, prioritizing data quality over pure model iteration.

What you'll learn

* **Structure unstructured data.** Map data and metadata into a queryable schema for images, videos, and point clouds.
* **Query datasets with the FiftyOne SDK**. Create complex views based on model predictions, labels, and custom tags. Use the FiftyOne to filter data based on logical conditions and confidence scores.
* **Visualize high dimensional embeddings**. Project features into lower dimensions to find clusters of similar samples. Identify data gaps and outliers using FiftyOne Brain.
* **Automate data curation.** Implement algorithmic measures to select diverse subsets for training. Reduce labeling costs by prioritizing high entropy samples.
* **Debug model performance.** Run evaluation routines to generate confusion matrices and precision recall curves. Visualize false positives and false negatives directly in the App to understand model failures.
* **Customize FiftyOne**. Build custom dashboards and interactive panels. Create specialized views for domain specific tasks.

**Prerequisites:**

* Working knowledge of Python and machine learning and/or computer vision fundamentals.
* All attendees will get access to the tutorials and code examples used in the workshop.
source: Meetup: Raleigh AI, ML & Computer Vision

title: MADTech Lecture: Greg Lindquist
description:
Greg Lindquist’s work examines the intersection of landscape, industry, and environmental change through painting, video, and research-based practice. Drawing on long-term projects including the Newtown Creek series in Brooklyn and more recent wildfire paintings, his work considers how contemporary landscapes are shaped by infrastructure, the forces of gentrification, extraction, and atmospheric conditions. A reception will follow in the Design Library in Brooks Hall, where Lindquist’s Study for Newtown Creek Series will be newly installed and on view as part of the NC State College of Design collection. Greg Lindquist, Heatwave (105 Wildfires Burn Across 35 Towns in Turkey), 2024
Oil, metallic, and iridescent pigment on linen on panel
Working between studio practice and field research, Lindquist documents sites where ecological systems and industrial processes overlap—locations where air, water, and built structures form complex environmental relationships. These investigations often involve collaboration with scientists, environmental organizations, and local communities, producing works that move between observation, documentation, mapping, and reimagined abstraction.
The lecture will trace the development of these projects over the past two decades, from early paintings of Brooklyn’s gentrification, essay-film experiments, to recent work addressing climate-driven wildfires. The talk coincides with the installation of Lindquist’s painting Study for Newtown Creek Series in the NC State College of Design Library. About the Artist  Greg Lindquist is a Brooklyn-based artist whose work examines landscape, ecology, and environmental change. Lindquist has exhibited widely, including at DC Moore Gallery, the Cameron Art Museum, the Brooklyn Academy of Music, the University of Arizona Museum of Art, and the North Carolina Museum of Art. He studied at the Whitney Museum of American Art Independent Study Program and holds degrees from NC State University and Pratt Institute

Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage. 

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country. 

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare. 

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

How to prepare:
We are excited to see you soon!

P.S. This is a call for young people from 13-25 years old who are interested in getting engaged with the Team ENOUGH program. If you are over the age of 25 please sign up for the Brady Welcome Session at https://www.mobilize.us/brady/event/274016/

title: Elk Knob State Park: Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt
description:
Join the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Elk Knob State Park. Journey through northern hardwood forest, follow winding mountain trails, and explore the unique ecosystems of this high-elevation park. Keep your eyes open—what signs of wildlife or weather-shaped landscapes will you uncover? Look for unique rocks that make Elk Knob a very special clue in North Carolina’s geologic history. Start at the Visitor Center and scan the QR code in your Actionbound app. Flyers with the QR code will be placed in the Park Office and on all park map kiosks. 

The adventures are available on the Actionbound app – a free download to your cellphone through your phone’s app store. There’s no need to create a profile and no personal data is collected with Actionbound. You simply find new hunts by searching for the park name or scanning the associated QR code posted for your park’s adventure.

This program is made possible through a partnership with the NC Science Trail (ncsciencetrail.org)! Visit their website for more Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunts being held in other NC State Parks and for other programs being offered throughout the state. 

This scavenger hunt is running now through April 30, 2026.

title: Visions of Freedom, Exhibit #1 (Iredell County Public Library: Main Branch-Statesville)
location: Iredell County Public Library, Main level
description:
Iredell County Public Library Commemorates 250 Years of Freedom with Year-Long Exhibit Series

The Iredell County Public Library will host a series of four local history exhibits throughout 2026 as part of America 250, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The inaugural exhibit, Visions of Freedom, will open to the public on January 12 on the Main floor of the Statesville branch library.

Visions of Freedom will focus on highlighting local landmarks, Revolutionary era residents, and important social movements that not only shaped the nation, but the Iredell County community. This free exhibit will offer a blend of information, images, and engaging interactive activities designed to appeal to visitors of all ages.

For more details about the exhibit series and upcoming local history events, please visit our website at https://iredell.lib.nc.us or contact Shellie Taylor at michelle.taylor@iredellcountync.gov

Statesville Library Hours: M-Th 8am-8pm, F & Sat 9am-6pm

title: Village of Pinehurst NCDNCR America 250 Exhibits
description:
The Village of Pinehurst will be displaying two of the NC Department of Natural & Cultural Resources exhibits throughout 2026.

"Forging a Nation" will be on display at the Cannon Park Community Center, 210 Rattlesnake Trail, Pinehurst, NC 28374.

"People of Colonial North Carolina" will be on display at Assembly Hall, 395 Magnolia Rd., Pinehurst, NC 28374.

The Given Memorial Library & Tufts Archives (150 Cherokee Road, Pinehurst, NC 28374) will also have smaller versions of the exhibits on display throughout the year and will rotate between the different exhibit subjects periodically.

title: "Making Our Voices Heard: North Carolinians Fighting for Civil Rights" Exhibit
description: This traveling exhibit tells the stories of seven everyday North Carolinians and extraordinary leaders — Gertrude Weil, Henry Owl, Joe Lewis, Abraham Galloway, Ronald Mace, James Hunter, and Willa Player — who petitioned, protested, and organized to expand democracy. The exhibit explores change, freedom, civic responsibility, and overcoming challenges by telling the story of a few North Carolinians who have raised their voices to call out injustice and fully participate in our democratic society.

title: Aquatic WILD
description:
Aquatic Wild is a program offered through the NC Wildlife Resources Commission. The North Carolina Aquarium at Fort Fisher and NC Sea Grant are facilitating this workshop.

The Aquatic WILD workshop is for formal and non-formal educators interested in teaching people about aquatic wildlife and ecology. Aquatic WILD materials build upon developments in wildlife conservation needs as well as advances in instructional methodology in Pre-K through 12th grade education.  

Participants in this 6-hour workshop receive the Aquatic WILD K-12 Curriculum & Activity Guide. The guide contains field investigations, In Step With STEM activity extensions, connections to wildlife careers, new activities on fish conservation and angling, and an increased focus on outdoor activities. Project Wild materials are provided free of charge by the NC Wildlife Resources Commission. 

The workshop at the Carolina Beach State Park will have a marine focus. Participants are eligible for Criteria I credit of NC OEE Environmental Education Certification and school teachers receive CEU credit. Homework option available.  

 

Location: Carolina Beach State Park

Cost: $25 per person 

 For additional workshop information, call 910-772-0546.

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

title: The Road Through “Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell”
description:
The Road Through Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell by photographer, oral historian, and U.S. Marine Corps veteran Theresa Scott. This deeply personal documentary exhibition explores the lived experiences of LGBTQIA+ veterans who served under restrictive military policies. 
Through intimate portrait photography paired with first-person oral histories, Scott brings forward stories long silenced by institutional policy and cultural pressure. Drawing on her own service, she offers viewers an unflinching look at the realities faced by service members who were expected to serve with honor while hiding essential parts of who they were. 
Exhibition Dates: February 1 – April 26, 2026
Artist Talk & Reception: March 26, 5:30–7:00 p.m.

Please register.

Visitors can view the exhibit free of charge any time the museum is open (M-Sun. 10 am-4 pm). Please stop by the Carriage ​House Visitor Center to gain admission. title: Right to Be's Bystander Intervention to Stop Online Harassment: How to Be an Ally When You Witness Abuse Online
description:
REGISTER HERE: https://righttobe.org/events/bystander-intervention-to-stop-online-harassment-how-to-be-an-ally-when-you-witness-abuse-online-7/ 




PEN America and Right to Be have partnered to provide training on how to intervene safely when you see a journalist attacked online. This training is also brought to you in partnership with the NYC Commission on Gender Equity, the Mayor’s Office of Equity and Racial Justice, and the NYC Commission on Gender Equity.


In this free, one-hour, interactive training, we’ll give you the tools you need to intervene safely and effectively in online abuse using Right To Be’s 5Ds of bystander intervention. First, we’ll talk through what online harassment is and how to identify abusive tactics. We’ll discuss the severe impact online abuse can have – on well being, livelihoods, and free expression – and how it’s drowning out voices that urgently need to be heard in public discourse. Then, we’ll share concrete strategies for how to distract, delegate, document, delay, or directly intervene in a way that is safe, effective, and centered on the needs of the person being targeted.

We’ll have time to practice so you can leave feeling more confident intervening the next time you see someone being abused online. We hope you’ll join us to learn how we can all band together to do your part to protect press freedom and defend the media from attacks on their independence, including online abuse and threats.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

title: April 9 - Workshop: Build a Visual Agent that can Navigate GUIs like Humans
description:
Raleigh AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
This hands-on workshop provides a comprehensive introduction to building and evaluating visual agents for GUI automation using modern tools and techniques.

**Date, Time and Location**

April 9, 2026 at 9 AM Pacific
Online. **[Register for the Zoom](https://voxel51.com/events/visual-agents-what-it-takes-to-build-an-agent-that-can-navigate-guis-like-humans-april-9-2026)**

Visual agents that can understand and interact with graphical user interfaces represent a transformative frontier in AI automation. These systems combine computer vision, natural language understanding, and spatial reasoning to enable machines to navigate complex interfaces—from web applications to desktop software—just as humans do. However, building robust GUI agents requires careful attention to dataset curation, model evaluation, and iterative improvement workflows.

Participants will learn how to leverage [FiftyOne](https://github.com/voxel51/fiftyone), an open-source toolkit for dataset curation and computer vision workflows, to build production-ready GUI agent systems.

What You'll Learn:

* **Dataset Creation & Management:** How to structure, annotate, and load GUI interaction datasets using the COCO4GUI standardized format
* **Data Exploration & Analysis:** Using FiftyOne's interactive interface to visualize datasets, analyze action distributions, and understand annotation patterns
* **Multimodal Embeddings:** Computing embeddings for screenshots and UI element patches to enable similarity search and retrieval
* **Model Inference:** Running state-of-the-art models like Microsoft's GUI-Actor to predict interaction points from natural language instructions
* **Performance Evaluation:** Measuring model accuracy using standard metrics and normalized click distance to assess localization precision
* **Failure Analysis:** Investigating model failures through attention maps, error pattern analysis, and systematic debugging workflows
* **Data-Driven Improvement:** Tagging samples based on error types (attention misalignment vs. localization errors) to prioritize fine-tuning efforts
* **Synthetic Data Generation:** Using FiftyOne plugins to augment training data with synthetic task descriptions and variations

*About the Speaker*

[Harpreet Sahota](https://www.linkedin.com/in/harpreetsahota204/) is a hacker-in-residence and machine learning engineer with a passion for deep learning and generative AI. He’s got a deep interest in RAG, Agents, and Multimodal AI.

title: State of AI - AI First or Obsolete
description:
Modern Web (Triangle)
​Most organizations are still treating AI like an add-on, layering it onto workflows that were never designed for it. The result is not transformation, it is marginal improvement dressed up as innovation. If your process looks the same after introducing AI, you are not ahead. You are just faster at doing the wrong things.
​
The real shift is AI-first, rebuilding how work gets done from the ground up. From collapsing cycle times to redefining software development and decision-making, this is where real advantage is created. We will break down what this looks like in practice and what it takes to get there at the State of AI event.

title: LaunchPad Incubator
location: Partners I – NC State University, Albright Entrepreneurship Garage Classroom
description:
NC State Innovation and Entrepreneurship has developed an incubator program to support early-stage startups. During the incubator, students will work on furthering their concepts through a variety of fundamental practices, such as doing customer discovery, exploring business modeling and thinking through commercialization strategy. This friendly, low-stakes and informal cohort is the perfect place to bounce ideas off one another and hold one another accountable for tangible next steps for your new venture.

The incubator occurs over a rolling 10-week period, with entrepreneurs joining on a drop-in basis. Student entrepreneurs are also eligible for micro funding. Funding can range from roughly $200 to $800 per student (up to $1,000 per team), depending on your venture and its needs.

While the cohort will meet for two hours every other week, the program gives students access to an asynchronous library of resources they can navigate at their own pace. Throughout the incubator period, participants will also be connected to mentorship and other forms of support. Every other week’s session will kick off with founder updates, including what’s working, roadblocks and goals for the week.

For more information about Launchpad and to apply, please visit the Launchpad web page.

The spring 2026 LaunchPad schedule and topics are below. Dates are subject to change.

Jan. 29: Intros and expectationsFeb. 12: Pivoting and deployment of your product/service in the face of extreme challengesFeb. 26: Customer discovery/market fitMarch 12: Short-form video content marketingMarch 26: Product scaling, production and crowdfundingApril 9: To be determinedApril 23: To be determined

title: PineCone Old Time Jam at Riparian
location: Riparian Provision Company, 1408 S. Saunders St., Raleigh, NC, 27603, United States
description:
Held on the 2nd Thursday of each month from 7-9 pm at the Riparian Provision Company (1408 South Saunders Street, Raleigh). This is an up to speed, gather in a circle kind of jam. It’s led by great players who work to make sure there’s space for everyone in the tunes. 
 
The leader picks a key (D, A and G are popular) and calls tunes in that key until it feels right to pick a new key and retune. The fiddlers traditionally call the tunes, but not always the jam leader. If you’re playing fiddle you should expect to be asked, “Hey, you got a good D tune?” While “no” is an acceptable answer, it’s good to have a tune in each key that you’d feel comfortable calling and kicking off. 
 
Whether you’re a first-time jammer or a veteran, you’re welcome to learn the tunes and play along, or just listen and observe! However, please note that this is not a “learning” or “slow” jam. Please remember – every jam is different! This jam tends to draw a good crowd, and it is open to musicians of all skill levels. Please help us make sure that newer players feel welcome. Also, big, mixed level jams can be challenging. Patience and kindness are appreciated! 
Recent tunes include: 
Fly Around (D) 
Soldier’s Joy (D) 
Whiskey Before Breakfast (D) 
Yellow Rose of Texas (D) 
Booth (A) 
John Brown’s Dream (A) 
Kitchen Girl (A) 
June Apple (A) 
Nail That Catfish to the Tree (G) 
Big Scotia (G) 
Elk River Blues (G) 
Jenny Run Away in the Mud in the Night (G)

title: My Fair Lady
location: Burning Coal Theatre, 224 Polk St, Raleigh, 27604
description:
My Fair Lady is a timeless musical that delves into the transformative power of language, identity, and social class in early 20th-century London. At the heart of the story is Eliza Doolittle, a spirited flower seller with a thick Cockney accent, who encounters the esteemed phonetics professor Henry Higgins. Fascinated by her unrefined speech and bold personality, Higgins makes a bold wager: he will teach Eliza to speak and behave like a proper lady of high society. 
As Eliza embarks on this challenging journey, the musical traces their evolving relationship through lessons in speech, manners, and self-discovery. Though they come from vastly different worlds, Higgins and Eliza form an unexpected bond that both challenges and changes them in profound ways.
—
Burning Coal Theatre Company is proud to announce its production of My Fair Lady, directed by Jerome Davis. My Fair Lady will run from April 9th to 26th, 2026, at the Murphey School, located at 224 Polk Street, Raleigh, NC 27604. Performances run on Thursdays through Saturdays at 7:30 p.m. and Sundays at 2:00 p.m. All tickets are $30, or $25 for seniors (65+), or $20 for students, teachers, and active military. People 18 and under can get a ticket to any performance for $5. April 10th is ‘College Night’, with $5 tickets for any college student with a valid ID. April 12th is ‘Pay What You Can’ day. Tickets and additional information can be found at www.burningcoal.org or by calling the box office at (919) 834-4001.

title: The Importance of Being Earnest by Oscar Wilde
description:
The Importance of Being Earnest, a Trivial Comedy for Serious People, is Oscar Wilde’s comedic play, which satirizes the conventions and manners of the late 19th century. Best friends Jack and Algernon each adopt fictional identities to escape social obligations. The plot unfolds with mistaken identities, romantic entanglements, clever wordplay and humorous social commentary.

The play's director is Danica Jenelle Jackson.

title: Classics Club: Joe Goodkin Performance
description:
The Classics Club invites you to attend a performance by Chicago-based singer-songwriter Joe Goodkin on Thursday, April 9, at 7:45 p.m. at Talley Student Union. Goodkin, who earned a Bachelor's of Arts in Classics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, created The Blues of Achilles, a musical adaptation of The Iliad, an epic poem by Greek poet Homer. The Blues of Achilles is a set of 17 original songs. It tells the story of The Iliad through the eyes of its characters: Achilles, Patroclus, Briseis, Helen, Priam and more. The performance evokes the original oral tradition of epic bards that stretches back millennia and frames the poem musically and narratively for modern audiences.

The performance will conclude at 9 p.m. A Q&A session will follow. Registration is required to attend.

Refreshments will be available.

title: Elk Knob State Park: Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt
description:
Join the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Elk Knob State Park. Journey through northern hardwood forest, follow winding mountain trails, and explore the unique ecosystems of this high-elevation park. Keep your eyes open—what signs of wildlife or weather-shaped landscapes will you uncover? Look for unique rocks that make Elk Knob a very special clue in North Carolina’s geologic history. Start at the Visitor Center and scan the QR code in your Actionbound app. Flyers with the QR code will be placed in the Park Office and on all park map kiosks. 

The adventures are available on the Actionbound app – a free download to your cellphone through your phone’s app store. There’s no need to create a profile and no personal data is collected with Actionbound. You simply find new hunts by searching for the park name or scanning the associated QR code posted for your park’s adventure.

This program is made possible through a partnership with the NC Science Trail (ncsciencetrail.org)! Visit their website for more Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunts being held in other NC State Parks and for other programs being offered throughout the state. 

This scavenger hunt is running now through April 30, 2026.

description:
Join TLC and Wake Audubon for this wonderful birding walk!
Our wonderful partners at Wake Audubon have joined TLC to lead a hike on the second Friday of each month at our Williamson Nature Preserve. Join this wonderful morning stroll and see what birds you can find. This hike will be just under 2 miles around the Two Pond Loop at the preserve. Please wear good walking shoes and layers, bring a water bottle, and binoculars if you have them. We suggest that you leave your furry friends at home for this hike as they may scare away wildlife viewing opportunities. This is a free event, but pre-registration is required.

 


If registration is full, please fill out the waitlist form here by April 8th at 10am.
Inclement Weather Policy: In the event of inclement weather, you will be contacted by email for a call on cancellation or postponement. At our Williamson and Brumley South Nature Preserves, due to the multi-use trail systems, we close the trails to the public if there has been rain to try and prevent erosion and detrimental impact. Please note that this event falls under this category and will be cancelled if the trails are closed. Please check your inboxes and spam folders prior to arriving!

Campsites at both Catawba River and Paddy's Creek accesses provide an opportunity to spend the night by the lake, with some sites accessible only by paddling. title: Visions of Freedom, Exhibit #1 (Iredell County Public Library: Main Branch-Statesville)
location: Iredell County Public Library, Main level
description:
Iredell County Public Library Commemorates 250 Years of Freedom with Year-Long Exhibit Series

The Iredell County Public Library will host a series of four local history exhibits throughout 2026 as part of America 250, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The inaugural exhibit, Visions of Freedom, will open to the public on January 12 on the Main floor of the Statesville branch library.

Visions of Freedom will focus on highlighting local landmarks, Revolutionary era residents, and important social movements that not only shaped the nation, but the Iredell County community. This free exhibit will offer a blend of information, images, and engaging interactive activities designed to appeal to visitors of all ages.

For more details about the exhibit series and upcoming local history events, please visit our website at https://iredell.lib.nc.us or contact Shellie Taylor at michelle.taylor@iredellcountync.gov

Statesville Library Hours: M-Th 8am-8pm, F & Sat 9am-6pm

Sign up using this link; a waitlist is available if the walk is full!

and scroll to the Wake Audubon event. 

Join Wake Audubon and Triangle Land Conservancy (TLC) for a morning of birding and exploring the Bailey and Sarah Williamson Preserve near the Wake County / Johnston County line. description: This traveling exhibit tells the stories of seven everyday North Carolinians and extraordinary leaders — Gertrude Weil, Henry Owl, Joe Lewis, Abraham Galloway, Ronald Mace, James Hunter, and Willa Player — who petitioned, protested, and organized to expand democracy. title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

description: Celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Halifax Resolves, the first official action by an entire colony recommending independence from Great Britain. Guest speakers will also give presentations on various topics. On Sunday, the living-history activities will continue. title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

description:

title: African American Libraries and Collections Exhibit

description:
Windows Into the Soul is an exhibition highlighting the powerful role that libraries, special collections and historical sites play in expanding access to African American and Afro-diasporic culture, knowledge and lived experiences. The exhibition will feature materials from Triangle-area libraries and special collections, including NC State and Shaw universities. It will showcase rare books, photographs, archival records, oral histories, creative works and community ephemera that illuminate the richness of African American life and expression.

The exhibition is part of the African American Cultural Center's celebration of National Library Week. Visitors of all backgrounds are welcome to come explore how libraries and archives preserve stories, expand access to knowledge and support deeper understanding across communities. The exhibit will be available to view April 8–10 from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m.

A closing reception that will feature remarks by exhibit partners will be held April 10 from noon to 2 p.m. Refreshments will be served at the reception. Student attendees will have a chance to win one of two Patron prize kits containing limited-edition AACC Library swag, a free book, library starter materials and more.

All are welcome to come see the exhibit and attend the reception.

title: Women's Only Handbuilding with Clay
location: The Joel Fund, 822 S White Street, Wake Forest, 27587
description:

Dates: Friday: 3/13, 3/20, 3/27, 4/10, 4/17, 4/24 MAKE UP: 5/1 (skip Good Friday, 4/3) 
Please Note: All classes and workshops are for Military Connected Individuals who are 18 years or older. This particular class is for military-connected women over 18 years or older. 
Create a one-of-a-kind collection of handbuilt ceramic art pieces! Projects include sculptural and functional items–examples of items we’ll make include a mug with a handle, a textured wall pocket hanging decoration, origami-inspired trinket dishes, and an owl-shaped votive luminary (see photos). These projects incorporate all the fundamental skills of handbuilding with clay: roll slabs, securely join clay components, add textures, pinching, coil building, and painting colorful underglazes onto your own pieces!Works will be fired off-site after the class is finished and will be available for pickup from the Joel Fund offices after class is over. No experience is necessary; your instructor will meet you where you are and provide the support you need to enjoy the creative process–the studio is fully accessible, participants will be able to stand or sit as desired, and accommodations are always available for any specific needs. Working with this medium provides a unique opportunity for sensory engagement and creative development–come connect to yourself and other makers as you find your way with clay! 
Please note, this class is for Women Only. 
We offer scholarships for those who cannot afford the registration fee. Email the Operation ART Program Manager at isabella@thejoelfund.org to receive the scholarship promo code with your name and email address.

title: Lunch and Learn with Andy Miller: EPA Endangerment Finding
description:
Join us to learn about the Endangerment Finding and what its rescission means (and doesn’t mean) for future GHG emissions.

In February, EPA rescinded its own legal authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions under the Clean Air Act, known as the Endangerment Finding. This action may have lasting implications for EPA’s future ability to regulate the GHGs that cause climate change. Hear more about the Finding, the implications of its rescission, and what might be next for GHG emissions from speaker, Andy Miller.

Andy Miller is CaSA's Practitioner-in-Residence (PIR) and an original author of the Endangerment Finding who spent 30 years working for the EPA.

Please register using NC State email address.

title: Teen Science Café: Monster Rockets
location: Downtown Raleigh, 11 West Jones Street, Raleigh, NC, 27601, United States
description:
This presentation compares the three biggest rockets ever built—the legendary Saturn V that took humans to the Moon, NASA’s powerful Space Launch System (SLS), and SpaceX’s ambitious Starship. Learn how these giants stack up in size, power, design and mission goals. Also, discover how each represents a different era of space exploration and our evolving plans to explore the Moon, Mars and beyond. 

About the presenter

Alan Rich is a retired scientist and engineer now working with NASA as a JPL Solar System Ambassador and occasional software tester and tech spin-off developer. He also represents the Los Angeles Astronomical Society. Alan enjoys taking deep topics such as astrophysics and rocket science and presenting them to any age group and education level in a way that’s entertaining and easy to understand. 


This program is recommended for participants ages 11–17. Cafés will be held in person at the Daily Planet Cafe AND streamed live on YouTube. Registration is required for online participation.

description:

Two hundred and fifty years after its birth, does America live up to its founding ideals? “Well, I Declare: America at 250” examines this question through songs that contend with the nation’s history, often as a call for change. North Carolina musicians Dawn Landes, Rissi Palmer, Jacob Sharp (Mipso) and Django Haskins (The Old Ceremony) will present songs new and old that speak to generations of struggle alongside a live reading of the Declaration of Independence by actor Mike Wiley.

title: My Fair Lady
location: Burning Coal Theatre, 224 Polk St, Raleigh, 27604
description:
My Fair Lady is a timeless musical that delves into the transformative power of language, identity, and social class in early 20th-century London. At the heart of the story is Eliza Doolittle, a spirited flower seller with a thick Cockney accent, who encounters the esteemed phonetics professor Henry Higgins. Fascinated by her unrefined speech and bold personality, Higgins makes a bold wager: he will teach Eliza to speak and behave like a proper lady of high society. 
As Eliza embarks on this challenging journey, the musical traces their evolving relationship through lessons in speech, manners, and self-discovery. Though they come from vastly different worlds, Higgins and Eliza form an unexpected bond that both challenges and changes them in profound ways.
—
Burning Coal Theatre Company is proud to announce its production of My Fair Lady, directed by Jerome Davis. My Fair Lady will run from April 9th to 26th, 2026, at the Murphey School, located at 224 Polk Street, Raleigh, NC 27604. Performances run on Thursdays through Saturdays at 7:30 p.m. and Sundays at 2:00 p.m. All tickets are $30, or $25 for seniors (65+), or $20 for students, teachers, and active military. People 18 and under can get a ticket to any performance for $5. April 10th is ‘College Night’, with $5 tickets for any college student with a valid ID. April 12th is ‘Pay What You Can’ day. Tickets and additional information can be found at www.burningcoal.org or by calling the box office at (919) 834-4001.

title: Opening Day– Exhibit: Battlefields to Backwoods-Soldiers Shaping Appalachia
description:
Join us for a powerful new exhibit celebrating America’s 250th anniversary. This immersive display explores how Revolutionary War veterans, including Transylvania's own Patriots such as Lambert Clayton, transitioned into pioneers in the former Cherokee lands that would one day become Transylvania County. The exhibit highlights land grants, frontier skills, and lasting legacies, all tying back to the fight for independence. 

Complementing the exhibit is our Revolutionary Era Garden, established in 2025 with support from the Transylvania County 250th Committee and America 250 NC, where families can engage in hands-on activities while learning about Colonial life and our Founding Fathers.

The exhibit will open in April and run through mid-October. Free and open to all.

title: Sexual Assault Awareness Month Denim Installation
description: Throughout April, the Women’s Center will have a Denim Day–themed installation in the Talley Student Union lobby gallery as part of Sexual Assault Awareness Month. This installation uses denim as a visual symbol of solidarity with survivors and challenges harmful myths and victim-blaming narratives. Visitors can engage with the display as an educational and reflective experience, learning about the history of Denim Day, the impact of sexual violence and ways to support survivors on campus. The installation will offer a consistent awareness-raising presence in one of the university’s most visible community spaces.

title: Spy Training 101: Decode a Secret Message
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
Pretend you’ve been recruited as a member of the Culper Spy Ring, and you need to know how to decipher a message written in invisible ink. Supplies include a paint brush, water, drying cloth, vitriol (diluted sulfuric acid), Thomas Jefferson cipher and “furnace box.” Read the clues to find the coin with a hidden message, reveal the message using the brush and vitriol, then use the cipher to decode the message.

Contact: Nancy Locquet Absillis, nancy.locquet@naturalsciences.org
