title: Geospatial Forum: Global Data for Local Action
description:
The Geospatial Forum will host a lecture by Ted Wong, a data scientist and research associate on the Urban Analytics team at the World Resources Institute's Ross Center for Sustainable Cities.

The World Resources Institute (WRI) is a large environmental nongovernmental organization that provides geospatial data and analyses to local governments to support sustainable urban planning. This talk will examine how WRI builds and deploys data products supporting city-level planning and decision-making for extreme heat, urban biodiversity and decarbonization. We will discuss theories of change, user research, project-level business models, strategies for mainstreaming, representation of uncertainty and all the technical considerations behind our data products.

title: Science Café: Illuminating AI Night
location: Nature Research Center, 121 West Jones Street, Raleigh, NC, 27601, United States
description:
Curious about what data science and AI bring to your life everyday? Join us for an evening discussing exciting local research from scientists at the NC Museum of Natural Sciences, UNC-Chapel Hill, UNC’s Renaissance Computing Institute (RENCI), NC State University, and beyond! You’ll learn about exciting research using artificial intelligence and data science methods to spark charismatic animal research, health-related research, participatory science opportunities in your backyard and across the globe in Galapagos, Puerto Rico, and beyond. The highlight of the evening will be the Science Cafe talk and its relevance to your daily life. You’ll leave the evening knowing how artificial intelligence benefits Museum research, art, and the world around us. 
Join us in person or watch the livestream of the Science Café beginning at 7:00 PM. 
Event Schedule
6:00pm-7:00pm: Meet local scientists and interact with themed exhibits to learn about their exciting research 
7:00pm, Science Cafe: Illuminating Artificial Intelligence: Using AI to increase the value of Museum specimens 
Our evening keynote pairs Dr. Chris Bizon, Director of Data Science and Analytics at RENCI and Dr. Lily Hughes, Research Curator of Ichthyology at the NC Museum of Natural Sciences and Research Assistant Professor at NC State University, highlighting how artificial intelligence illuminates our understanding of the Museum’s ichthyology collections. 
About the Illuminating AI Series  
The Illuminating AI series transforms cutting-edge research into accessible public conversations, showcasing the work of scientists at the Renaissance Computing Institute (RENCI), UNC-Chapel Hill, NC State University, the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences (NCMNS) and Google AI for Nature. 
This initiative examines the science underlying today’s AI headlines, guiding audiences through the technology that drives artificial intelligence while investigating its effects on the natural environment. 
The Illuminating AI series is a collaborative partnership between RENCI at UNC Chapel Hill and the North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences.

title: "Logistics of Liberty" A250 Presentation
location: N.C. Transportation Museum, Roundhouse Orientation Room
description:
During the American Revolution, supplying the Continental Army was one of its greatest challenges, and moving provisions from place to place was a constant struggle. The critical role of rough roads, winding rivers, and thousands of draft animals is often overlooked in the story of the Revolution. Discover how hundreds of North Carolinians were called into service to transport essential goods across the state and beyond.

Join Nathan Schultz for a fascinating presentation on this lesser-known side of the Revolution, including his own experiences portraying an ox driver along part of Henry Knox’s historic route through hands-on interpretation of teamster work. If you need assistance or have any questions before registering, contact Matthew McCarthy at matthew.mccarthy@dncr.nc.gov or 704-605-6282.

title: Elk Knob State Park: Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt
description:
Join the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Elk Knob State Park. Journey through northern hardwood forest, follow winding mountain trails, and explore the unique ecosystems of this high-elevation park. Keep your eyes open—what signs of wildlife or weather-shaped landscapes will you uncover? Look for unique rocks that make Elk Knob a very special clue in North Carolina’s geologic history. Start at the Visitor Center and scan the QR code in your Actionbound app. Flyers with the QR code will be placed in the Park Office and on all park map kiosks. 

The adventures are available on the Actionbound app – a free download to your cellphone through your phone’s app store. There’s no need to create a profile and no personal data is collected with Actionbound. You simply find new hunts by searching for the park name or scanning the associated QR code posted for your park’s adventure.

This program is made possible through a partnership with the NC Science Trail (ncsciencetrail.org)! Visit their website for more Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunts being held in other NC State Parks and for other programs being offered throughout the state. 

This scavenger hunt is running now through April 30, 2026.

title: Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt!
description: Embark on the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Lake James State Park! Located in Burke and McDowell counties 50 miles northeast of Asheville, Lake James State Park includes two areas to access this picturesque lake that are perfect for boating, swimming, and fishing. Campsites at both Catawba River and Paddy's Creek accesses provide an opportunity to spend the night by the lake, with some sites accessible only by paddling. Trails include bike trails at Paddy's Creek, the kid-friendly Holly Discovery Trail, the historic Overmountain Victory Trail, and the Fonta Flora State Trail.

description:

Park at Boone Fork Parking Area (milepost 299.9 on the Blue Ridge Parkway), find the flyer by the map at the start of the trailhead, scan the QR code in the Actionbound app, and start completing the Grandfather Mountain State Park bound! The QR code is also attached to this event if you'd like to scan earlier and see what adventure you'll be going on.

This scavenger hunt takes you up Daniel Boone Scout Trail to Flat Rock View, which is 3.6 miles round trip. The hike is moderately strenuous, and climbs 1,050 feet up to Flat Rock View. 

This is a self-guided hike, please wear appropriate hiking shoes and dress for the weather.

There are no bathrooms at Boone Fork Parking Area.

Join an Aquarium naturalist for a guided walk on the beach as you search for sandpipers, plovers, willets, and other shoreline specialists. Learn how to spot key field marks, identify birds by behavior and habitat, and discover how tides influence where shorebirds feed and rest. Along the way, you’ll pick up expert birding tips and enjoy a special up-close encounter with one of our bird ambassadors. Binoculars provided, or bring your own!

$15 non member / $13.50 aquarium member

Ages 10 and up. Ages 10 - 17 must be accompanied by a participating adult

title: Visions of Freedom, Exhibit #1 (Iredell County Public Library: Main Branch-Statesville)
location: Iredell County Public Library, Main level
description:
Iredell County Public Library Commemorates 250 Years of Freedom with Year-Long Exhibit Series

The Iredell County Public Library will host a series of four local history exhibits throughout 2026 as part of America 250, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The inaugural exhibit, Visions of Freedom, will open to the public on January 12 on the Main floor of the Statesville branch library.

Visions of Freedom will focus on highlighting local landmarks, Revolutionary era residents, and important social movements that not only shaped the nation, but the Iredell County community. This free exhibit will offer a blend of information, images, and engaging interactive activities designed to appeal to visitors of all ages.

For more details about the exhibit series and upcoming local history events, please visit our website at https://iredell.lib.nc.us or contact Shellie Taylor at michelle.taylor@iredellcountync.gov

Statesville Library Hours: M-Th 8am-8pm, F & Sat 9am-6pm

description: This traveling exhibit tells the stories of seven everyday North Carolinians and extraordinary leaders — Gertrude Weil, Henry Owl, Joe Lewis, Abraham Galloway, Ronald Mace, James Hunter, and Willa Player — who petitioned, protested, and organized to expand democracy. The exhibit explores change, freedom, civic responsibility, and overcoming challenges by telling the story of a few North Carolinians who have raised their voices to call out injustice and fully participate in our democratic society.

title: Celebrating Our Colonial Roots - Online Plant Sale
location: Pick up 5/1/26 at Greenhouses behind Building N
description: The Brunswick County Master Gardeners Volunteer Association will hold an online plant sale starting on April 17, 2026 and running until April 24, 2026 with pick up day on May 1, 2026. This event celebrates the important colonial history of Brunswick County  through education on herbs, flowers, vines, shrubs and small trees which thrive here. Plants featured are those which our Colonial ancestors would have encountered along our coast and the Cape Fear River which are native to our region and support pollinators. Also featured will be plants from seeds which colonists brought with them from Europe and plants which recognize the contributions and life celebrations of the Gullah Geechee people who were enslaved in Africa to work the rice plantations along the Cape Fear River. This online plant sale celebrates the cultural traditions  found in gardening in our coastal region of the State.

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. description:
NC State’s Terrain Dance Project will present Themes of Gathering, a collection of new site-specific choreographic works at The Corner on Centennial Campus at 2 p.m. April 17 and 7 p.m. April 18. The Terrain Dance Project is a site-specific dance company dedicated to the creation and performance of choreographed and improvised dance works in nontraditional spaces, including dance film projects.

This interdisciplinary performance investigates The Corner as a site of gathering and identity, featuring live musicians and choreography by co-director Amy Love Beasley, guest artists Jill Guyton Nee and Anabelle Scarborough and NC State senior Annabelle Sharp. Select works explore the intersection of dance and science, inspired by work by NC State's Gage Lab and the North Carolina Sweetpotato Commission. This project is supported by an arts and science grant from the Office of Interdisciplinary Programs and Arts NC State.

In case of inclement weather on the scheduled performance dates, the performances will take place April 19 at 2 and 7 p.m.

title: Two Lights for Tomorrow 2026
description:
Two Lights for Tomorrow' Will Shine in Communities Across Brunswick County Friday, April 18

 

As we approach the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence in 2026, Brunswick County residents are requested to participate in a powerful moment of reflection and unity and to honor the spirit of cooperation and courage that helped ignite the American Revolution.

On the night of April 18, 1775, Paul Revere and William Dawes rode out from Boston to alert their fellow patriots of the movement of the British regulars. A prearranged signal — two lanterns in the tower of Christ Church — warned that the British troops were traveling via the Charles River. Other riders joined Revere and Dawes, creating a network across the Massachusetts countryside which eventually led to the NC/SC border where a rider informed Isaac Marion, proprietor of the Boundary House and brother of Swamp Fox Francis Marion.

Launched in 2025, Two Lights for Tomorrow was initiated by America 250 NC to encourage communities across North Carolina to illuminate two lights on notable buildings and homes, commemorating the renowned ride through the colonies.

Brunswick Town Chapter NSDAR continues that effort on Friday, April 18, 2026, as we urge businesses and homes throughout the county to shine two lights on their structures or in windows.

description:
Join the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Elk Knob State Park. Journey through northern hardwood forest, follow winding mountain trails, and explore the unique ecosystems of this high-elevation park. Keep your eyes open—what signs of wildlife or weather-shaped landscapes will you uncover? Look for unique rocks that make Elk Knob a very special clue in North Carolina’s geologic history. Start at the Visitor Center and scan the QR code in your Actionbound app. Flyers with the QR code will be placed in the Park Office and on all park map kiosks. 

The adventures are available on the Actionbound app – a free download to your cellphone through your phone’s app store. There’s no need to create a profile and no personal data is collected with Actionbound. You simply find new hunts by searching for the park name or scanning the associated QR code posted for your park’s adventure.

This program is made possible through a partnership with the NC Science Trail (ncsciencetrail.org)! Visit their website for more Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunts being held in other NC State Parks and for other programs being offered throughout the state. 

This scavenger hunt is running now through April 30, 2026.

description:
Iredell County Public Library Commemorates 250 Years of Freedom with Year-Long Exhibit Series

The Iredell County Public Library will host a series of four local history exhibits throughout 2026 as part of America 250, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The inaugural exhibit, Visions of Freedom, will open to the public on January 12 on the Main floor of the Statesville branch library.

Visions of Freedom will focus on highlighting local landmarks, Revolutionary era residents, and important social movements that not only shaped the nation, but the Iredell County community. This free exhibit will offer a blend of information, images, and engaging interactive activities designed to appeal to visitors of all ages.

For more details about the exhibit series and upcoming local history events, please visit our website at https://iredell.lib.nc.us or contact Shellie Taylor at michelle.taylor@iredellcountync.gov

title: Celebrating Our Colonial Roots - Online Plant Sale
location: Pick up 5/1/26 at Greenhouses behind Building N
description: The Brunswick County Master Gardeners Volunteer Association will hold an online plant sale starting on April 17, 2026 and running until April 24, 2026 with pick up day on May 1, 2026. This event celebrates the important colonial history of Brunswick County  through education on herbs, flowers, vines, shrubs and small trees which thrive here. Plants featured are those which our Colonial ancestors would have encountered along our coast and the Cape Fear River which are native to our region and support pollinators. Also featured will be plants from seeds which colonists brought with them from Europe and plants which recognize the contributions and life celebrations of the Gullah Geechee people who were enslaved in Africa to work the rice plantations along the Cape Fear River. This online plant sale celebrates the cultural traditions  found in gardening in our coastal region of the State.

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

There is a maximum of one dog per handler. This hike is for adults only.  Dogs must be non-reactive and on a 6ft fixed-length (not retractable) leash at all times. This is a free event, but preregistration is required.

 



If registration is full, please fill out the waitlist form here by April 16th at noon.

title: Triangle Unified Bridge Brigade: 3rd Saturday of the month

description: Come join Engaged Defenders for Democracy as we partner with the Overpass Coalition to have a Unified Bridge Brigade that covers bridges in the Triangle and beyond on the third Saturday of the month. We will have protectors on multiple bridges to show that we are not going away, we are not backing down, and we support our neighbors and workers. We also are uniting all of us over billionaires. We will have message about peace, unity, and defending our Constitution. We will host a Visibility Brigade event where drivers see our protectors and signs as they drive under overpasses in Durham, Raleigh, Cary, Pittsboro, and Chapel Hill. (we are coordinating with 10 other states). Please use the SignUp Genius to sign up for the bridge you will attend: https://www.signupgenius.com/go/10C0549A5AA23A1F8C43-61318184-cultivating#/ Even in cooler temperatures, sunburn and dehydration can be a problem. Please bring water, snacks, sun screen, a hat, sunglasses, and clothing suitable for the weather. The bridges get very breezy. You can learn details by visiting our website. https://durhamresistancehub.com/btfsite We will ask people to bring American flags and smaller signs if they have cars and pedestrians on the bridge. Please also bring Rainbow flags, Mexican flags, and Palestine flags. Please tell your friends to come. People loved driving under bridge after bridge seeing our protectors up there sharing a unified message. Please be part of this next coordinated event! Please join our Substack: https://substack.com/profile/115484101-engaged-defenders-4-democracy For more ED4D Mobilize Events: https://www.mobilize.us/engagedefendersfordemocracy/ Have accessibility questions? title: Art in the Park: Cardboard Illustrations
description: Join us for a hands-on painting and illustration workshop led by Caroline Paul. We'll use repurposed cardboard to share memories and experiences through imagery and text, inspired by Paul's own work — seen around Winston-Salem and now officially installed through a Public Art Council grant in Miller, Washington, and Lockland Parks. Participants can explore expressive figures, animals, shapes, and messages on cardboard, an affordable and familiar material that offers an inviting surface for experimentation and communication. This all-ages workshop encourages play, reflection, and creative confidence. No experience needed, just curiosity and a desire to make something meaningful together.

description:
Please join Engaged Defenders for Democracy every Saturday from 10am-11:30am with signs to protect our democracy and protest the violations to our Constitution. We will meet at the YMCA at 218 West Morgan St.

We need to fight for our democracy and stop and prevent future cuts that are hurting many. Bring friends! Bring signs that show your concern or are a call to action. Please avoid triggering images like swastikas.

See you every Saturday morning engaging drivers & pedestrians in Downtown Durham!

Please join our Substack: https://substack.com/profile/115484101-engaged-defenders-4-democracy

title: Drawing Meditation with Maureen O’Neill
description:
This workshop designed by Maureen O’Neill offers a variety of exercises to help participants connect to and engage with the present moment. Through guided mark making (drawing and painting), participants learn to shift focus to their touch and breath and experience how a beautiful line or color can bring them into a meditative place that is both healing and creative.

Supplies are included and no art experience is necessary. This workshop encourages and supports the strength and wisdom of the intuitive spirit.

title: ERA - Guided Forest Therapy Hike - Confluence Natural Area
location: 4214 Highland Farm Rd, Hillsborough, NC 27278, USA
description:
Registration is required - Tickets drop on March 1st at 8:00am!
Price: $4
*Ticket prices directly support the work of the Eno River Association. Thank you for your support!


Forest Therapy (sometimes known as Forest Bathing or Shinrin-Yoku) broadly means taking in the forest atmosphere with all of one's senses. Not simply a walk in the woods; it is the conscious and contemplative practice of being immersed in the sights, sounds, and smells of the forest. During your walk, Aimee Vandemark will guide you through invitations to awaken your senses, slow down, be present, and reconnect with the nature and rhythm of your surroundings.


Meet at the pavilion beside the parking lot. This hike will take approximately two hours (sometimes less, sometimes more). Please feel free to bring water and snacks. Wear comfortable, weather-appropriate clothing and shoes. Well-behaved dogs are welcome as long as they are under your control and on a 6-foot leash. Restrooms are available on-site.


The address is 4214 Highland Farm Rd, Hillsborough, NC 27278.

From Hillsborough take Hwy 86 North away from town 1.6 miles from US70. Turn left on Coleman Loop 1.1 miles. Turn left on Highland Farm Rd 2.4 miles. The Confluence is on the left. There is a large sign and a gravel driveway. From northern Orange County take Hwy 86 south after passing Walnut Grove Church Rd take the first right on Kenion Rd 1.7 miles. Turn right on Highland Farm Rd 0.6 miles. The Confluence is on the left. There is a large sign and a gravel driveway.

title: Exploring Your Own Backyard
description: In celebration of Earth Day, join the Tobacco Farm Life Museum to explore ways that you can engage with nature, right in your own backyard! Learn more about the world around you from community partners like the North Carolina Bluebird Society, the Wilson County Beekeepers, and the Wilson County Master Gardeners. Participate in games and hands-on activities, create crafts, and learn about how people in the past interacted with nature in their backyards. Don't forget to check out the traveling exhibit "Saving Our Wildflowers," on loan from the North Carolina Botanical Gardens in the gallery!

title: Legends & Landmarks: Paintings and Drawings by James C. Horton
description: In commemoration of America's 250th, the Bellamy Mansion Museum is hosting an art exhibition by local artist James C. Horton, which includes over 40 original paintings and drawings that highlight historic scenes and places from around the region and country that help tell America's story. Visitors can view the exhibit free of charge any time the museum is open (M-Sun. 10 am-4 pm). Please stop by the Carriage ​House Visitor Center to gain admission. Art is available for purchase and an Artist's Reception will be held on February 27th (6-8pm). Visit bellamymansion.org/exhibits for more information or email info@bellamymansion.org if you have questions.

title: Patch-a-Palooza at Vance Birthplace
description:
Join us on Saturday, April 18th for a day of sensory learning and fun at Vance Birthplace! Patch-a-Palooza welcomes families with K-8th grade children to try their hands at various historic activities from making butter to playing historic games. Each learning station has a stamp, and children who earn a stamp from every station will receive a Vance Birthplace patch along with their take-home crafts. This is a great opportunity for children to learn about life in Western North Carolina in the 1800s while working on their fine motor, artistic, and critical thinking skills.

Admission is $7 per child to cover the cost of craft supplies. Adults may enter for free unless they choose to participate in the crafts. Enter through the visitor center to pay admission and receive stamp cards. This event is appropriate for all ages but is primarily geared toward elementary and middle grade learners.

For more information, email us at vance@dncr.nc.gov or give us a call at (828) 645-6706!

title: Sachets in the Historical Park
description: Plants and flowers have their own language and different combinations of them can be used to send messages in secret. Used for medicine, hygiene, and bug repellents during the American Revolution, come to the Historical Park and create your own sweet-smelling sachet. Our costumed interpreters will show you how. FREE. All ages welcome. Drop-in.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

description:
KMHM is excited to present Women at the Edge of War: Carolina Piedmont's Heroines of the American Revolution. This exhibit highlights the daily courage and civic work of women in the Carolinas, whose efforts were essential to Revolutionary resistance and survival on the southern frontier.

The exhibit will run from Feb. 17, 2026 to May 30, 2026. The museum is open Tues-Sat, 10-4. Admission is free. Check out kingsmountainmuseum.org or call 704-739-1019 for more information.

description:
Join us for the 2nd annual Jones Lake Exploration Expo! It will be an exciting day of exploration and discovery at Jones Lake State Park! A variety of agencies and organizations will transform the park into a dynamic hub of interactive STEM activities and displays. Each table will feature a unique, hands-on experience designed to spark curiosity and engage minds of all ages. This family-friendly event promises fun, learning, and inspiration for kids and parents alike as you journey through our natural world.

title: GGC Adventure Series: Lake Raleigh Paddle
description:
Back for another year of inspiring adventures in nature, this season of the Greenway Gear Collective Adventure Series will feature Adventure Race themed outings.
Each event will focus on one of the disciplines of adventure racing: traditionally mountain biking, orienteering (map and compass navigation), and paddling (canoe or kayak) and will take place at or around Lake Raleigh. Beginners or veterans alike will be in excellent hands with each adventure led by Debra and Jeff Rezeli, experts with over 11 years of adventure racing experience.
Register for each event here.

For those who love a goal to build towards...
The series will build skills in advance of a local practice 3-hour adventure race in May and the option to register and participate in a 5-hour adventure race hosted by Broad Run Offroad on June 13 & 14 at Lake Anna State Park in Spotsylvania, VA.
For more information on adventure racing, check out the US Adventure Racing Association website.

title: Hidden Battleship Tour
description:
Hidden Battleship is for the explorer at heart! Join us for an afternoon on a unique, behind-the-scenes tour of unrestored areas on the Battleship. Organized into small groups, the participants are led to areas in the bow, third deck, and below, and the superstructure, including all the way to the very top! This program requires climbing ladders, crossing high hatches, and going through tight/confined spaces. The tour is limited to ages 16 and older.

title: The Student Art Sale
description:
Liven up your space or gift original art by supporting NC State's talented student artists at the Student Art Sale.

Since 2015, Arts NC State has hosted its annual art sale event, showcasing the talent and creativity of students.  The art sale welcomes submissions from all students, whether they study engineering, chemistry, media art design technology or any other field, making the event one of the nation's premier university art showcases. Every purchase at the art sale empowers students, fueling their artistic journey. Since its start, our art sale event has contributed over $100,000 to student artists, making a real impact on their lives and careers.

Join us in supporting and investing in the next generation of artists whose talents transcend disciplines.

The art sale will be held at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design.

The museum has limited parking. We strongly encourage guests to carpool or walk to the museum. Please view available parking options before your visit to the museum. ﻿

title: Treasures at Tea Time
description: Please join us as we raise a teacup to our founding mothers. Step back in time for an enjoyable afteroon while hearing from the remarkable women who stood beside America's founding fathers. We will meet women of wit, strength, and influence that helped shape a nation. You will enjoy an elegant array of food and tea while celebrating history. While not required ,please feel free to wear your best colonial or regency period clothing or your favorite tea party hat. Proceeds from ticket sales will go towards an America 250! Scholarship to be presented to a student of Craven County Community College.

title: VOICES FROM THE PAST - Celebrating AMERICA250 NC
description:
How are you celebrating AMERICA250NC?
Step into history with a spirited stroll through Charlotte’s past.
 
 VOICES FROM THE PAST is a unique living history event that invites guests to explore Charlotte’s historic cemeteries, Settlers', Elmwood, and Pinewood. Along the way, you’ll meet 25 costumed storytellers who bring history to life, sharing the amazing stories of the men and women who helped make Charlotte into what it is today.

 VOICES FROM THE PAST is not a guided tour. It is a living history event unlike anything you've ever been to.  The storytellers are at the grave of the person they are portraying. Visitors will interact with the portrayers as they stroll from one to another at their own pace.

AMERICA250  NC will be spotlighted throughout the day with "milestones" of Charlotte's history beginning with its Declaration of Independence on May 20, 1775.
 

VOICES FROM THE PAST is where Charlotte's 250-year history comes alive for the day, one story at a time. Whether you are a Charlotte native or new to the city, you will learn enjoy hearing the stories. And, we promise that before the end of the day, you will say, "WOW, I didn't know that"!

 This year, we have the honor of her Majesty Queen Charlotte helping us celebrate this special anniversary. Bring your cameras for a selfie with the Queen!

title: Wild About Wildflowers
description:
April is the time of year when many of the wildflowers begin to bloom at Elk Knob State Park! Enjoy an NCSciFest event at Elk Knob by hiking with a Park Ranger on the Summit Trail to survey wildflowers. We will be using a couple of identification methods such as an ID guide and an app called iNaturalist. All observations will be photographed and uploaded to iNaturalist and NC State Park’s Natural Resource Inventory Database.

No survey and identification experience required to participate in this program! The Summit Trail is 1.9 miles one way and is moderate to strenuous. We will be meeting in the Summit Trail parking lot to begin. Dress appropriately to hike and bring water.

title: Terrain Dance Project Concert: Themes of Gathering
description:
NC State’s Terrain Dance Project will present Themes of Gathering, a collection of new site-specific choreographic works at The Corner on Centennial Campus at 2 p.m. April 17 and 7 p.m. April 18. The Terrain Dance Project is a site-specific dance company dedicated to the creation and performance of choreographed and improvised dance works in nontraditional spaces, including dance film projects.

This interdisciplinary performance investigates The Corner as a site of gathering and identity, featuring live musicians and choreography by co-director Amy Love Beasley, guest artists Jill Guyton Nee and Anabelle Scarborough and NC State senior Annabelle Sharp. Select works explore the intersection of dance and science, inspired by work by NC State's Gage Lab and the North Carolina Sweetpotato Commission. This project is supported by an arts and science grant from the Office of Interdisciplinary Programs and Arts NC State.

In case of inclement weather on the scheduled performance dates, the performances will take place April 19 at 2 and 7 p.m.

title: Mapping Instincts
location: Frank Thompson Hall - Kennedy-McIlwee Studio Theatre
description: In 1998, the neuroscientist Jaak Panksepp published a book classifying seven primary affective systems or, more simply, emotional developmental states. Mapping Instincts is our collective exploration of these concepts at play in our bodies and minds. Directed by Mia Self.

title: The Importance of Being Earnest by Oscar Wilde
description:
The Importance of Being Earnest, a Trivial Comedy for Serious People, is Oscar Wilde’s comedic play, which satirizes the conventions and manners of the late 19th century. Best friends Jack and Algernon each adopt fictional identities to escape social obligations. The plot unfolds with mistaken identities, romantic entanglements, clever wordplay and humorous social commentary.

The play's director is Danica Jenelle Jackson.

title: 1776 Musical - Sherman Edwards and Peter Stone
location: Raleigh Little Theatre , Cantey V. Sutton Theatre
description:
It’s the summer of 1776, and the nation is ready to declare independence… if only our founding fathers can agree to do it! 1776 follows John Adams of Massachusetts, Benjamin Franklin of Pennsylvania and Thomas Jefferson of Virginia as they attempt to convince the members of the Second Continental Congress to vote for independence from the shackles of the British monarchy by signing the Declaration of Independence.

The seminal event in American history blazes to vivid life in this most unconventional of Broadway hits. Celebrate the semiquincentennial of the United States at 1776!

Music and Lyrics by Sherman Edwards
Book by Peter Stone
Based on a concept by Sherman Edwards
Original Production Directed by Peter Hunt
Originally Produced on the Broadway Stage by Stuart Ostrow

Directed by Patrick Torres

1776 is presented through special arrangement with Music Theatre International (MTI). All authorized performance materials are also supplied by MTI. www.mtishows.com

title: Spy Training 101: Decode a Secret Message
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:

title: Elk Knob State Park: Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt
description:
Join the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Elk Knob State Park. Journey through northern hardwood forest, follow winding mountain trails, and explore the unique ecosystems of this high-elevation park. Keep your eyes open—what signs of wildlife or weather-shaped landscapes will you uncover? Look for unique rocks that make Elk Knob a very special clue in North Carolina’s geologic history. Start at the Visitor Center and scan the QR code in your Actionbound app. Flyers with the QR code will be placed in the Park Office and on all park map kiosks. 

The adventures are available on the Actionbound app – a free download to your cellphone through your phone’s app store. There’s no need to create a profile and no personal data is collected with Actionbound. You simply find new hunts by searching for the park name or scanning the associated QR code posted for your park’s adventure.

This program is made possible through a partnership with the NC Science Trail (ncsciencetrail.org)! Visit their website for more Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunts being held in other NC State Parks and for other programs being offered throughout the state. 

This scavenger hunt is running now through April 30, 2026.

title: Visions of Freedom, Exhibit #1 (Iredell County Public Library: Main Branch-Statesville)
location: Iredell County Public Library, Main level
description:
Iredell County Public Library Commemorates 250 Years of Freedom with Year-Long Exhibit Series

The Iredell County Public Library will host a series of four local history exhibits throughout 2026 as part of America 250, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The inaugural exhibit, Visions of Freedom, will open to the public on January 12 on the Main floor of the Statesville branch library.

Visions of Freedom will focus on highlighting local landmarks, Revolutionary era residents, and important social movements that not only shaped the nation, but the Iredell County community. This free exhibit will offer a blend of information, images, and engaging interactive activities designed to appeal to visitors of all ages.

For more details about the exhibit series and upcoming local history events, please visit our website at https://iredell.lib.nc.us or contact Shellie Taylor at michelle.taylor@iredellcountync.gov

title: Celebrating Our Colonial Roots - Online Plant Sale
location: Pick up 5/1/26 at Greenhouses behind Building N
description: The Brunswick County Master Gardeners Volunteer Association will hold an online plant sale starting on April 17, 2026 and running until April 24, 2026 with pick up day on May 1, 2026. This event celebrates the important colonial history of Brunswick County  through education on herbs, flowers, vines, shrubs and small trees which thrive here. Plants featured are those which our Colonial ancestors would have encountered along our coast and the Cape Fear River which are native to our region and support pollinators. Also featured will be plants from seeds which colonists brought with them from Europe and plants which recognize the contributions and life celebrations of the Gullah Geechee people who were enslaved in Africa to work the rice plantations along the Cape Fear River. This online plant sale celebrates the cultural traditions  found in gardening in our coastal region of the State.

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

title: Alligator River Wildlife Paddle (Manns Harbor)
description:
Join NCWF’s Wildlife Habitat Stewards of Northeastern NC Chapter and Coastal Kayak for a guided paddle through Alligator River National Wildlife Refuge on Sunday, April19, from 10 a.m. to 12 p.m. As you glide through the calm refuge waters, keep an eye out for alligators, river otters, and a wide variety of birds and other species enjoying their natural habitats. 
Established in 1984, the refuge protects the rare pocosin wetlands, unique ecosystems built on deep peat soils and covered with low, shrubby vegetation. The area also includes swamp forest and is bordered by rich marshland. This vast protected landscape supports thriving populations of black bears and wintering waterfowl, and it’s one of the only places in the world where you might spot endangered Red Wolves in the wild. 
Enjoy this unforgettable two-hour adventure for just $45 per person, which includes experienced guides, a kayak, and all necessary gear. Both single and double kayaks are available. 
**After you register here, you’ll receive a confirmation email with a link for payment and reservation of your kayak with Coastal Kayak.**

title: Forest Bathing: A Guided Journey Into Nature's Wisdom
description:

The experience will encourage you to slow down, awaken your senses and reconnect with the natural world in a meaningful way. Inspired by the Japanese practice of shinrin-yoku and supported by growing scientific research, forest bathing promotes relaxation, improved mood and enhanced well-being.

As you meander through the natural areas of the JC Raulston Arboretum, you’ll be gently guided through a series of mindfulness practices and nature-based invitations designed to foster presence, curiosity and a deeper sense of connection.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

location: Boone Fork Parking Area, Milepost 299.9 on the Blue Ridge Parkway

Park at Boone Fork Parking Area (milepost 299.9 on the Blue Ridge Parkway), find the flyer by the map at the start of the trailhead, scan the QR code in the Actionbound app, and start completing the Grandfather Mountain State Park bound! title: StoryWalk®  - "The hike by: Alison Farrell
location: Carvers Creek State Park – Long Valley Farm Access
description: StoryWalk® is simply a book and a walking path combined.  In 2007, Anne Fergusson with the Vermont Department of Health had the idea to combine literacy and exercise. Teaming up with the Kellog Hubbard Library in Montpelier they attached laminated pages from a children’s book onto wooden posts.  In the ten years since, StoryWalks have gone up in all 50 states and at least 11 countries. The pages are affixed to metal sign stakes and a trail instantly becomes even more fun for children and book-lovers of all ages. StoryWalks® will usually remain up for one-to-two weeks along easy trails about one mile or less. The story featured this time is called "The Hike" by Alison Farrell. It will be along our Cypress Point Loop Trail.

title: Visions of Freedom, Exhibit #1 (Iredell County Public Library: Main Branch-Statesville)
location: Iredell County Public Library, Main level
description:
Iredell County Public Library Commemorates 250 Years of Freedom with Year-Long Exhibit Series

The Iredell County Public Library will host a series of four local history exhibits throughout 2026 as part of America 250, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The inaugural exhibit, Visions of Freedom, will open to the public on January 12 on the Main floor of the Statesville branch library.

Visions of Freedom will focus on highlighting local landmarks, Revolutionary era residents, and important social movements that not only shaped the nation, but the Iredell County community. This free exhibit will offer a blend of information, images, and engaging interactive activities designed to appeal to visitors of all ages.

For more details about the exhibit series and upcoming local history events, please visit our website at https://iredell.lib.nc.us or contact Shellie Taylor at michelle.taylor@iredellcountync.gov

Statesville Library Hours: M-Th 8am-8pm, F & Sat 9am-6pm

title: "Making Our Voices Heard: North Carolinians Fighting for Civil Rights" Exhibit
description: This traveling exhibit tells the stories of seven everyday North Carolinians and extraordinary leaders — Gertrude Weil, Henry Owl, Joe Lewis, Abraham Galloway, Ronald Mace, James Hunter, and Willa Player — who petitioned, protested, and organized to expand democracy. The exhibit explores change, freedom, civic responsibility, and overcoming challenges by telling the story of a few North Carolinians who have raised their voices to call out injustice and fully participate in our democratic society.

title: Celebrating Our Colonial Roots - Online Plant Sale
location: Pick up 5/1/26 at Greenhouses behind Building N
description: The Brunswick County Master Gardeners Volunteer Association will hold an online plant sale starting on April 17, 2026 and running until April 24, 2026 with pick up day on May 1, 2026. This event celebrates the important colonial history of Brunswick County  through education on herbs, flowers, vines, shrubs and small trees which thrive here. Plants featured are those which our Colonial ancestors would have encountered along our coast and the Cape Fear River which are native to our region and support pollinators. Also featured will be plants from seeds which colonists brought with them from Europe and plants which recognize the contributions and life celebrations of the Gullah Geechee people who were enslaved in Africa to work the rice plantations along the Cape Fear River. This online plant sale celebrates the cultural traditions  found in gardening in our coastal region of the State.

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

title: Research Up Close: Constructed Facilities Lab Tour
description:

You'll be guided by CFL researchers who can show you all of their coolest toys and tell you about the importance of their research and its impact on the world.
This is an educational experience, but it is also an incredibly entertaining peek into one of the most hands-on and immediately recognizable research experiences on campus. Their machines might be complicated, but when you get to watch a decommissioned bridge pillar break under a shake test, it is as fascinating to watch as it is to instantly understand why it matters.
Slots are limited, so please register to attend the tour.

title: The Art and Science of Plant Care
description:
Caring for plants is both an art and a science — part intuition, part know-how. Every gardener, from beginner to expert, faces the same essential questions: When should I prune? How much should I water? What’s the best way to plant, fertilize or repot? In this class, Bryce Lane will bring decades of horticultural expertise to demystify these everyday tasks, showing you not just what to do but why it works.

Over eight weeks, you’ll explore the fundamental practices that keep gardens thriving, learning how to perform each one with confidence and purpose. You’ll uncover the science behind good technique — understanding how soil, water, nutrients and plant biology interact — while also developing the practical judgment that comes only with experience.

Each session will focus on one key aspect of plant care, building a complete toolkit for growing healthier, more resilient plants in any garden setting.

title: Civic Hacking for Affordable Housing
description:
Code with the Carolinas - Triangle
Join volunteers at Code with the Carolinas as we help the [National Zoning Atlas](https://www.zoningatlas.org/) (NZA) team include North Carolina and South Carolina in their nationwide zoning atlas. "The National Zoning Atlas aims to depict key aspects of zoning codes in an online, user-friendly map." The Atlas aims to provide data for better solutions in transportation, environmental, and especially affordable housing policy.

Affordable housing proponents have long recognized zoning policies as barriers to affordable housing. To improve zoning policies, we first need to better understand the current state of zoning across the United States. Code with the Carolinas is helping this cause by joining the National Zoning Atlas to gather zoning data for North and South Carolina.

This is a multi-dimensional project grounded in data science with an end-goal of contributing to a nationally influential dataset. Our current work session activities focus on internet search and integrating data from multiple sources. The project as a whole has occasional opportunities for U/X and outreach and opportunities to learn about machine learning and natural language processing through the work of the NZA team. Volunteering on this project will provide excellent exposure to the foundations of civic data science, with a focus on GIS data.

Even if you're new to this project and/or civic tech volunteering, you're welcome to join the meeting. Visitors are always welcome and no technical skills are needed. You can learn more about the project on our [Slack Workspace](https://join.slack.com/t/codeforthecarolinas/shared_invite/zt-1kxuwu05x-3KxOpkOYjAuN5yuOAH8ROg) in the #project-zoning-atlas channel.

Meetings start with brief introductions. New volunteers are offered a personal orientation, often in a breakout room, while experienced volunteers get right to work. By the end of the session, both groups of volunteers are working together. We also contribute to the project through asynchronous work and informal work sessions.

Meetings are on the Jitsi platform and the link is provided before each meeting. If you will be joining on mobile, install the Jitsi app in advance [https://jitsi.org/downloads/](https://jitsi.org/downloads/) .

Learn more at [codewiththecarolinas.org](codeforthecarolinas.org) or reach out to info@codewiththecarolinas.org

All activities of Code with the Carolinas, a project of [Social Good Fund](https://www.socialgoodfund.org/), follow our [Code of Conduct](https://share.mailbox.org/ajax/share/0d32d5f905f8fd49d5e80395f8fd47f2b59ce3ef8b335f72/1/8/Nzg/NzgvMTkx) and are subject to this [Volunteer Waiver of Liability](https://share.mailbox.org/ajax/share/06dd62200e6b28426b137e0e6b2848fb901487014f72cd16/1/8/Nzg/NzgvMTE2).

The Emerging Designers Textile howcase highlights the work of senior textile design students in the fashion and textile design (FTD) program at the Wilson College of Textiles, celebrating the culmination of a semester-long capstone experience rooted in exploration, experimentation and refinement. Designers navigate the balance between creative freedom and creative discipline while leveraging access to state-of-the-art labs and studios. Collections span home textiles, apparel, fiber art and more. 

The Emerging Designers Textile Showcase will be held at the Textiles Campus on Centennial Campus.

The Textile Showcase Opening is on Sunday, April 19, from 3 to 5 p.m. The event is open to the public and free for all.

The Textile Showcase will also be open:
- Monday, April 20, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
- Tuesday, April 21, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
- Wednesday, April 22, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

title: Grandfather Mountain Scavenger Hunt
location: Boone Fork Parking Area, Milepost 299.9 on the Blue Ridge Parkway
description:
Join us all month long for NC April Science Festival with this self-guided scavenger hunt up to Flat Rock View. Park at Boone Fork Parking Area (milepost 299.9 on the Blue Ridge Parkway), find the flyer by the map at the start of the trailhead, scan the QR code in the Actionbound app, and start completing the Grandfather Mountain State Park bound! The QR code is also attached to this event if you'd like to scan earlier and see what adventure you'll be going on.

This scavenger hunt takes you up Daniel Boone Scout Trail to Flat Rock View, which is 3.6 miles round trip. The hike is moderately strenuous, and climbs 1,050 feet up to Flat Rock View. 

This is a self-guided hike, please wear appropriate hiking shoes and dress for the weather.

There are no bathrooms at Boone Fork Parking Area.

title: StoryWalk®  - "The hike by: Alison Farrell
location: Carvers Creek State Park – Long Valley Farm Access
description: StoryWalk® is simply a book and a walking path combined.  In 2007, Anne Fergusson with the Vermont Department of Health had the idea to combine literacy and exercise. Teaming up with the Kellog Hubbard Library in Montpelier they attached laminated pages from a children’s book onto wooden posts.  In the ten years since, StoryWalks have gone up in all 50 states and at least 11 countries. The pages are affixed to metal sign stakes and a trail instantly becomes even more fun for children and book-lovers of all ages. StoryWalks® will usually remain up for one-to-two weeks along easy trails about one mile or less. The story featured this time is called "The Hike" by Alison Farrell. It will be along our Cypress Point Loop Trail.

title: Visions of Freedom, Exhibit #1 (Iredell County Public Library: Main Branch-Statesville)
location: Iredell County Public Library, Main level
description:
Iredell County Public Library Commemorates 250 Years of Freedom with Year-Long Exhibit Series

The Iredell County Public Library will host a series of four local history exhibits throughout 2026 as part of America 250, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The inaugural exhibit, Visions of Freedom, will open to the public on January 12 on the Main floor of the Statesville branch library.

Visions of Freedom will focus on highlighting local landmarks, Revolutionary era residents, and important social movements that not only shaped the nation, but the Iredell County community. This free exhibit will offer a blend of information, images, and engaging interactive activities designed to appeal to visitors of all ages.

For more details about the exhibit series and upcoming local history events, please visit our website at https://iredell.lib.nc.us or contact Shellie Taylor at michelle.taylor@iredellcountync.gov

Statesville Library Hours: M-Th 8am-8pm, F & Sat 9am-6pm

description:
Join NC State for a celebration of sustainability accomplishments on Tuesday, April 21, 2026. This annual event honors the people, projects and progress that advance sustainability at NC State.

The celebration will include a Sustainability Showcase starting at 8:30 a.m. where you can browse student displays on sustainability-related projects.  Students,  student organizations, departments and researchers are invited to share their sustainability-focused research and projects in a science-fair style format. title: Village of Pinehurst NCDNCR America 250 Exhibits
description:
The Village of Pinehurst will be displaying two of the NC Department of Natural & Cultural Resources exhibits throughout 2026.

"Forging a Nation" will be on display at the Cannon Park Community Center, 210 Rattlesnake Trail, Pinehurst, NC 28374.

"People of Colonial North Carolina" will be on display at Assembly Hall, 395 Magnolia Rd., Pinehurst, NC 28374.

The Given Memorial Library & Tufts Archives (150 Cherokee Road, Pinehurst, NC 28374) will also have smaller versions of the exhibits on display throughout the year and will rotate between the different exhibit subjects periodically.

title: "Making Our Voices Heard: North Carolinians Fighting for Civil Rights" Exhibit
description: This traveling exhibit tells the stories of seven everyday North Carolinians and extraordinary leaders — Gertrude Weil, Henry Owl, Joe Lewis, Abraham Galloway, Ronald Mace, James Hunter, and Willa Player — who petitioned, protested, and organized to expand democracy. The exhibit explores change, freedom, civic responsibility, and overcoming challenges by telling the story of a few North Carolinians who have raised their voices to call out injustice and fully participate in our democratic society.

title: Celebrating Our Colonial Roots - Online Plant Sale
location: Pick up 5/1/26 at Greenhouses behind Building N
description: The Brunswick County Master Gardeners Volunteer Association will hold an online plant sale starting on April 17, 2026 and running until April 24, 2026 with pick up day on May 1, 2026. This event celebrates the important colonial history of Brunswick County  through education on herbs, flowers, vines, shrubs and small trees which thrive here. Plants featured are those which our Colonial ancestors would have encountered along our coast and the Cape Fear River which are native to our region and support pollinators. Also featured will be plants from seeds which colonists brought with them from Europe and plants which recognize the contributions and life celebrations of the Gullah Geechee people who were enslaved in Africa to work the rice plantations along the Cape Fear River. This online plant sale celebrates the cultural traditions  found in gardening in our coastal region of the State.

title: Earth Day Craft
description: Create your own planet in celebrate of the rock we call home! Craft supplies will be available all week long in the Visitor Center while it is open. After you create your Earth, turn it into the office staff to be put on display.

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

title: Traveling Exhibit from NC Botanical Gardens: Bee-Hold the Humble Pollinator
description: Take a journey into world of one our amazing pollinators, Bees! This traveling exhibit from NC Botanical Gardens explains some of the science behind bees and includes an interactive specimen case!

title: A Creek in Carolina: Artworks by Bobby C. Martin
description: A Creek in Carolina : Artworks by Bobby C. Martin will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. Nationally recognized artist Bobby C. Martin (Muscogee Creek) presents a solo exhibition tracing the pathways connecting ancestral Mvskoke homelands to Indian Territory. Drawing from family photographs and archival materials, Martin weaves encaustic, collage, maps, hymns, and personal imagery to reframe histories of forced removal as stories of resilience, survival, and continuity—inviting viewers to reflect on their own family histories and the enduring presence of Mvskoke people.

title: Legends & Landmarks: Paintings and Drawings by James C. Horton
description: In commemoration of America's 250th, the Bellamy Mansion Museum is hosting an art exhibition by local artist James C. Horton, which includes over 40 original paintings and drawings that highlight historic scenes and places from around the region and country that help tell America's story. Visitors can view the exhibit free of charge any time the museum is open (M-Sun. 10 am-4 pm). Please stop by the Carriage ​House Visitor Center to gain admission. Art is available for purchase and an Artist's Reception will be held on February 27th (6-8pm). Visit bellamymansion.org/exhibits for more information or email info@bellamymansion.org if you have questions.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

title: Stories Told by Breath: Native American Voices in North Carolina
description:
Stories Told by Breath will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. This exhibition celebrates the creativity, memory, and cultural continuity of Native American artists connected to North Carolina. 

The exhibition brings together a rich range of media—clay, beadwork, textiles, printmaking, regalia, sculpture, and multimedia—woven with storytelling to form a vibrant experience of artistic practice in North Carolina.

Artists include Senora Lynch (Haliwa-Saponi), Karina McMillan (Lumbee), Harlen Chavis (Lumbee), Aaron Baumgardner (Catawba),Coda Cavalier (Occaneechi Band of the Saponi Nation), Amy Postoak (Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians)& Johnny Postoak (Muscogee Creek)of Three Sisters Designs, Rhiannon “Skye” Tafoya (Eastern Band of Cherokee & Santa Clara Pueblo), Joshua Adams (Eastern Band of Cherokee), Idalis Dial (Coharie), Tim Locklear (Lumbee), NC State students Ashtyn Thomas (Lumbee) and Victoria Wilson (Haliwa-Saponi), Gwen Locklear (Lumbee) and Alexandra Williams portrait photographs of Powwows at Dix Park. Together, these artists explore heritage, craft, and storytelling as a living continuum of creativity, connecting ancestral knowledge with contemporary expression.

title: The House of Ideas: Plants in Art Exhibition
location: Gregg Museum of Art & Design, Cabaniss Gallery
description: The House of Ideas: Plants in Art will be on exhibit in the Cabaniss Gallery in the Historic Chancellor’s Residence every Tuesday-Saturday until May 31, 2026. This exhibition is a participatory learning lab that uncovers the artistic representation of plants in our lives and in the natural world. It features objects from the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Collection that depict the roles of plants from nourishment and communal living to the scientific study of human health. The House of Ideas offers a relaxing room for botanical sketching and a self-guided tour of the museum’s garden.

title: The Old Settler's Trail
description: Join Ranger Fields and step back in time to explore an old road that early settlers took to enter Danbury. This will be a challenging loop hike with several creek crossings, totaling approximately 3.5 miles. Hiking attire, water, and a hiking pole are recommended. This experience is for the adventurous. To sign up for this hike or for any questions, email Jacob.fields@ncparks.gov

title: Through Our Eyes, In Our Hands: Prioritizing Indigenous Knowledge in Museums
description:
Through Our Eyes, In Our Hands: Prioritizing Indigenous Knowledge in Museums will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until June 27, 2026. This exhibition foregrounds Native perspectives on the stewardship of cultural belongings and the history and future of repatriation. This exhibition transforms the museum into a site of learning, self-examination, and responsibility.

Visitors are guided through the intertwined histories of museum collecting, cultural consultation, and the journey to repatriation. Archival materials, personal accounts, and community-based narratives offer insight into the significance of the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (NAGPRA) and the ongoing work beyond its legal requirements. Rather than presenting repatriation as a transactional process, this exhibition emphasizes its cultural, spiritual, emotional, and relational dimensions—its power to restore connections and honor ancestors and communities.

title: Women at the Edge of War: Carolina Piedmont's Heroines of the American Revolution
description:
KMHM is excited to present Women at the Edge of War: Carolina Piedmont's Heroines of the American Revolution. This exhibit highlights the daily courage and civic work of women in the Carolinas, whose efforts were essential to Revolutionary resistance and survival on the southern frontier.

The exhibit will run from Feb. 17, 2026 to May 30, 2026. The museum is open Tues-Sat, 10-4. Admission is free. Check out kingsmountainmuseum.org or call 704-739-1019 for more information.

title: Art2Wear: Open Studio
description:
Students in the Art2Wear studio will offer a behind-the-scenes look at what goes into making this annual show so iconic. Join us for a opportunity to see the student designers at work, ask them questions and see the details that make up their final collections. 

Art2WearTM (A2W) is an educational event where students gain experience by coordinating and producing an annual wearable art production. Young designers are challenged to imagine, create and inspire by expressing their point of view through wearable art. This highly anticipated show fuses the talents of several departments in the College of Design and beyond, exposing student designers to the broader fields of wearable art, digital media production and fashion. A2W attracts attendees from all over the Triangle by encouraging participation through engaging the student body, the Raleigh community and the broader design industry.

title: Fashion Week Screening and Artist Talk: Whose Woods Are These
location: James B. Hunt Jr. Library, Teaching and Visualization Lab
description:
Please attend a screening of Whose Woods Are These, a seven-minute animated short created entirely from woven fabric by Associate Professor Kate Nartker. Presented as part of the NC State  Fashion Week, this special event marks a full-circle moment as the film returns to NC State following a year-long festival run.

The animation is composed of jacquard-woven textiles that were scanned and sequenced frame by frame, transforming cloth into a moving image. Inspired by a 19th-century family story set in northwest Ohio’s Great Black Swamp, the film reimagines themes of disappearance, wilderness and wonder through a tactile, fiber-based lens.

Following the screening, Nartker will share a brief presentation on the weaving and animation process and the story that inspired the work.  Nartker will also answer questions.

title: Kiana Bonollo: How I Built a Fashion Career Using Social Media
location: Wilson College of Textiles, W. Duke Kimbrell Atrium
description:
What began as posting sewing projects on YouTube evolved into a multi-platform business built on digital sewing patterns, online education and brand partnerships. In this talk, Kiana Bonollo '21, a content creator and patternmaker, will discuss how she identified a gap in the market, listened to her audience and turned technical design skills into scalable digital products.

She will explore how social media has transformed entrepreneurship in the fashion industry: lowering marketing barriers, creating direct access to consumers and opening new career paths beyond traditional corporate roles. Students will learn how to think strategically about social platforms, whether as influencers, entrepreneurs or designers building their own brands.

The event is free but has limited capacity. Registration is required. NC State students and employees have priority registration (open now!). Registration will be open to the public on April 13 if spots remain.

title: *IN-PERSON* SF/F Group
description:
Durham Writers Group
We will be at the People's Solidarity Hub at 1809 Chapel Hill Rd, Durham. This venue does not serve food or drink, but feel free to bring your own. There is a kitchenette for our use, but be sure to clean up afterwards. The space might be a little cozy; please consider masking or staying home if you have a respiratory ailment.

This sub-group focuses on Speculative Fiction, including Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror. If you have anything that falls under that category — be it short story, poem, novel-in-progress or screenplay — then come! We'd love to hear from you.

Our format allows each reader 15 minutes to present their work aloud, followed by approximately 20 minutes of feedback from the other attendees. To ensure fairness, each attendee is limited to 1 minute of Initial Feedback time. During that period, the author remains silent. Next, we have a 5 minute Free-For-All discussion about the work -- then the author may speak. (We usually get through three readers.)

Though not required, in order to receive more in-depth feed-back, readers may post their work in advance on our Google Group:
https://groups.google.com/d/forum/durham-sff-writers-group

We ask that participants keep their comments constructive and respectful, focusing on what works or doesn't work in the piece.

We also ask that readers provide a warning, both on the Google Group and during the meeting, if their story features content that some readers might find upsetting. This includes descriptions of violence or sexual content.

title: Last Week of Spring Semester
description: Lab tests, semester project reports and presentations are permissible during the final week of classes. Papers and homework may have a due date during the final week of classes only if scheduled in the syllabus. However, in order for students to prepare for final examinations, faculty members may not assign other tests, quizzes or additional papers during the final week of classes. Assignments should not have a due date during the final exam period unless the assignment constitutes a part of the final exam. Exceptions to this policy must be approved in advance by the department head and the dean of the college involved. Students should contact the appropriate instructor or department head if they believe an assignment is not in compliance with this regulation.

title: Sexual Assault Awareness Month Denim Installation
description: Throughout April, the Women’s Center will have a Denim Day–themed installation in the Talley Student Union lobby gallery as part of Sexual Assault Awareness Month. This installation uses denim as a visual symbol of solidarity with survivors and challenges harmful myths and victim-blaming narratives. Visitors can engage with the display as an educational and reflective experience, learning about the history of Denim Day, the impact of sexual violence and ways to support survivors on campus. The installation will offer a consistent awareness-raising presence in one of the university’s most visible community spaces.

title: Spy Training 101: Decode a Secret Message
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
Pretend you’ve been recruited as a member of the Culper Spy Ring, and you need to know how to decipher a message written in invisible ink. Supplies include a paint brush, water, drying cloth, vitriol (diluted sulfuric acid), Thomas Jefferson cipher and “furnace box.” Read the clues to find the coin with a hidden message, reveal the message using the brush and vitriol, then use the cipher to decode the message.

Contact: Nancy Locquet Absillis, nancy.locquet@naturalsciences.org

title: Elk Knob State Park: Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt
description:
Join the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Elk Knob State Park. Journey through northern hardwood forest, follow winding mountain trails, and explore the unique ecosystems of this high-elevation park. Keep your eyes open—what signs of wildlife or weather-shaped landscapes will you uncover? Look for unique rocks that make Elk Knob a very special clue in North Carolina’s geologic history. Start at the Visitor Center and scan the QR code in your Actionbound app. Flyers with the QR code will be placed in the Park Office and on all park map kiosks. 

The adventures are available on the Actionbound app – a free download to your cellphone through your phone’s app store. There’s no need to create a profile and no personal data is collected with Actionbound. You simply find new hunts by searching for the park name or scanning the associated QR code posted for your park’s adventure.

This program is made possible through a partnership with the NC Science Trail (ncsciencetrail.org)! Visit their website for more Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunts being held in other NC State Parks and for other programs being offered throughout the state. 

This scavenger hunt is running now through April 30, 2026.

description: Embark on the Curious Minds Adventure Scavenger Hunt at Lake James State Park! description:
