title: *IN-PERSON* SF/F Group
description:
Durham Writers Group
We will be at the People's Solidarity Hub at 1809 Chapel Hill Rd, Durham. This venue does not serve food or drink, but feel free to bring your own. There is a kitchenette for our use, but be sure to clean up afterwards. The space might be a little cozy; please consider masking or staying home if you have a respiratory ailment.

This sub-group focuses on Speculative Fiction, including Science Fiction, Fantasy and Horror. If you have anything that falls under that category — be it short story, poem, novel-in-progress or screenplay — then come! We'd love to hear from you.

Our format allows each reader 15 minutes to present their work aloud, followed by approximately 20 minutes of feedback from the other attendees. To ensure fairness, each attendee is limited to 1 minute of Initial Feedback time. During that period, the author remains silent. Next, we have a 5 minute Free-For-All discussion about the work -- then the author may speak. (We usually get through three readers.)

Though not required, in order to receive more in-depth feed-back, readers may post their work in advance on our Google Group:
https://groups.google.com/d/forum/durham-sff-writers-group

We ask that participants keep their comments constructive and respectful, focusing on what works or doesn't work in the piece.

We also ask that readers provide a warning, both on the Google Group and during the meeting, if their story features content that some readers might find upsetting. This includes descriptions of violence or sexual content.

location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

How to join:
Please join our virtual welcome session with this link

Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage. 

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country. 

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare. 

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

We are excited to see you soon!

title: NC Trail Days 2026
location: Yadkin Valley Heritage & Trails Visitor Center
description: NC Trail Days returns to the towns of Elkin and Jonesville, North Carolina on the first weekend of June. This four day event celebrates the 'Great Trails State' along with the abundant opportunities for outdoor recreation in this part of the Blue Ridge foothills. The event features an array of guided hikes, several of which are along the NC Mountains-to-Sea Trail and the Overmountain Victory National Historic Trail, as well as multiple paddle trips on the Yadkin River. Many of the hikes are themed and focus on unique regional history such as the popular hidden moonshine stills hike, or the naturalist hiking series which offers glimpses of the area's ecology and milltown history. In addition to guided and self-guided hikes, the festival offers rock climbing at nearby Stone Mountain and Pilot Mountain State Parks, cycling, trail races, outdoor gear vendors, live music and more. Nearly all the events are free to attend but may require registration. These details will be released with the schedule in Spring of 2026. Check out www.nctraildays.com for more info until then, and we hope to see you there!

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

description:

The onslaught of news, the chaos coming out of the White House – it’s all meant to overwhelm us. It’s a deliberate strategy to sow confusion and make us believe we are powerless to fight back.

The antidote: Coming together in community to process what’s happening, to sift through what’s important and what’s just noise, and coalesce around strategies for fighting back.

title: Conversations on Catawba History and Arts With Aaron Baumgardner
location: Gregg Museum of Art & Design, Main Lobby
description: Join the Gregg Museum of Art & Design for an illuminating discussion with contemporary artist Aaron Baumgardner (Catawba). In conjunction with the exhibition Stories Told by Breath: Native American Voices in North Carolina, Baumgardner will offer insights into the themes and techniques that define his work. As a Catawba artist with a background in ecology, Baumgardner’s work preserves ancestral pottery and revitalizes basketry traditions, ensuring they thrive for future generations. Through traditional arts, he explores the interconnectedness of the land, culture and history, honoring the resilience of the Catawba people. The presentation will conclude with a Q&A session, inviting attendees to engage directly with the artist about his creative practices. After the presentation, attendees can explore the exhibitions at the Gregg and connect further with Baumgardner.

title: Ashe County America 250th Celebration
description:
Come celebrate the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States on the grounds of the Museum of Ashe County History.

On this day, set aside to celebrate, learn, and reflect, visitors will have the opportunity to chat with living historians about the American Revolution, see craft demonstrations, enjoy children's activities, and listen to historic lectures.

At 11 a.m. the Daniel Boone Chapter of the Daughters of the American Revolution will read the Declaration of Independence. Later that day, at 1 p.m., historian Michael C. Hardy will give a lecture on his newest book, "Western North Carolina and Eastern Tennessee and the American Revolution."

Visitors are encouraged to tour the exhibits within the Museum of Ashe County History to learn more about their local heritage.

This event is FREE and open to the public.

title: America 250 Stars and Stripes
description:
Wilmington Conservatory’s 2026 performance will take the stage on June 6th at the Wilson Center in Downtown Wilmington. Travel through our nations art history this summer.

The Wilmington Conservatory presents "America 250: Stars and Stripes", a vibrant mixed repertory showcase celebrating the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence through dance and music. Step right up for a captivating journey through the eras of American art, from early storytelling traditions to the trailblazers who shaped our nation’s artistic heritage, and discover how history inspires art and how art, in turn, shapes history.

Experience iconic works such as Rodeo, inspired by modern dance pioneer Agnes de Mille and the American frontier; Gershwin’s Rhapsody in Blue from the 1920s Jazz Era; a tribute honoring the U.S. military; songs from Elvis Presley echoing the spirit of Martin Luther King Jr.’s historic speech; an intertribal showcase featuring Native American tribes of the Southeastern United States; and a grand finale original ballet of Stars and Stripes Forever, with music from John Philip Sousa and Hershey Kay, inspired by George Balanchine. Plus, enjoy the styles and sounds of Scott Joplin, Benny Goodman, Isadora Duncan, Gus Giordano, Alvin Ailey, Aretha Franklin, Gene Kelly, Judy Garland, and more, brought to life by the dancers of Wilmington Conservatory of Fine Arts and guided by original story narration.

As our nation and community come together to mark this Quarter Millennium, this moving museum of American art invites audiences to celebrate the creativity legacy of our nation, honoring 250 years of the United States and the artists who continue to inspire the next generation.

description:
Gather your family and friends for a day at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design to celebrate the rich and diverse cultures of Native American communities. All are welcome to come learn, create and experience tradition through hands-on artmaking, games, artist demonstrations, storytime and engaging performances. Join us for:

Hands-on artmaking and traditional games from 3 to 6 p.m. (Attendees can participate in various art activities and crafts and engage in various games.)Artist demonstrations from 3:15 to 3:45 p.m. and 5 to 5:30 p.m (Aaron Baumgardner (Catawba), and Johnny (Muscogee Creek) and Amy Postoak (Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians) will conduct demonstrations.)Storytime from 3:45 to 4 p.m. and 5:30 to 5:45 p.m. (Storytime sessions will occur on the lawn.)An American Indian cultural performance from 4 to 5 p.m. (Ryan (Lumbee), Idalis (Coharie) and Raven Dial (Lumbee) will perform.)This event is in partnership with the NC State American Indian Advisory Council and is designed to honor, respect, and share the heritage of Native people. Come spend the afternoon at the Gregg Museum to celebrate and experience belonging.

title: Bald Eagle Search Paddle with Two Sisters Adventure Company
description:
Join Two Sisters Adventure Company for a Bald Eagle Search Paddle at Jordan Lake State Recreation Area, hosted on select dates throughout 2026. Jordan Lake is one of the best Bald Eagle viewing locations in the region. You will paddle past multiple nesting areas in search of our majestic national bird. While sightings are not guaranteed, Bald Eagles are most common in the areas they visit. Your guide will help you identify and answer questions about Bald Eagles and other birds in the area. All participants should have basic kayaking skills, due to the duration on the water this trip is considered intermediate. Pre-registration is required. Participants will launch from the Farrington Point Access. The trip will last approximately 4 hours. Trips will take place on the following dates:

Thu, Mar 26, 9am-1pm.Sun, Apr 26, 8:30am-12:30pm.Sat, May 9, 8am-12pm.Sat, May 30, 8am-12pm.Sun, Jun 7, 8am-12pm.Two Sisters works with all guests to make trips as accessible as possible. Please contact them with any specific accessibility requests so they can ensure they have all the necessary equipment and staff. Free parking is available at the Farrington Point Canoe Launch. No pets are allowed. The cost is $60 per person, and pre-registration is required. Single-person kayaks are provided. Participants ages 15 and older are welcome.

This event is part of our Chatham Celebrates America 250 initiative. See more America 250 events. See more Chatham Sports Alliance events.

Two Sisters acknowledges that the land on which this camp takes place is the ancestral land of the Skaruhreh/Tuscarora, Lumbee, Mánu: Yį Įsuwą (Catawba), Occaneechi, Shakori, and Cheraw Nations. As a part of their mission, they honor and respect the history and significance this land holds for these Nations’ past, present, and future. To find out more about the Native People and Lands where you live and recreate, visit this map.

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution.

Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

Please join Engaged Defenders for Democracy on Mondays from 7:30-9 at the corner of Franklin St & Elliott Rd in Chapel Hill for a weekly, peaceful, nonpartisan protest and call to action. Free parking at the Church of Reconciliation, 110 N Elliott Rd.

Across the political spectrum, Americans are disillusioned by leaders who put power over people. We gather to build community, spark hope, and inspire action.

Bring a friend. Bring a sign. Speak up for immigrant rights, free speech, healthcare, social security, the environment, the Constitution and the rule of law, reproductive freedom, job and funding cuts, and the many, many other issues close to our hearts. Bonus points for signs that encourage others to move beyond honking and help turn awareness into action.  We often hand out fliers to stopped cars & pedestrians with information about relevant actions folks can take to support their community and defend democracy. We also have a Signal chat for regular attenders. If you are interested in either of these opportunities, ask around for Wendy.

This will be a POSITIVE and nonviolent demonstration. We are here to protect our democracy. We are standing up for what we believe in. We want to inspire people to join us and grow our movement!

Please bring positive signs supporting the movement and resisting what is happening in our country!

Please no mocking signs, no swastikas

We are excited to see you there and stand together for our country!

See you every Monday afternoon engaging drivers in Chapel Hill!

title: Flags of the American Revolution
description: The 250th Anniversary of our great nation is upon us, and there are many aspects of our history that we may not know.   For example, our American flag has evolved and changed many times over the years.  Have you ever wondered what our very first flag looked like, and how and why it changed during the time of our American Revolution?  Members of the New Bern Chapter of the Sons of the American Revolution will display and share some of the exciting history behind our flag, as well as other interesting information, during their presentation on June 8, 2026, at 4:30 pm.  For more information, please contact us at 252-566-3772 or at lagrange@neuselibrary.org.

title: A Creek in Carolina: Artworks by Bobby C. Martin
description: A Creek in Carolina : Artworks by Bobby C. Martin will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. Nationally recognized artist Bobby C. Martin (Muscogee Creek) presents a solo exhibition tracing the pathways connecting ancestral Mvskoke homelands to Indian Territory. Drawing from family photographs and archival materials, Martin weaves encaustic, collage, maps, hymns, and personal imagery to reframe histories of forced removal as stories of resilience, survival, and continuity—inviting viewers to reflect on their own family histories and the enduring presence of Mvskoke people.

description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

title: Stories Told by Breath: Native American Voices in North Carolina
description:
Stories Told by Breath will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. This exhibition celebrates the creativity, memory, and cultural continuity of Native American artists connected to North Carolina. 

The exhibition brings together a rich range of media—clay, beadwork, textiles, printmaking, regalia, sculpture, and multimedia—woven with storytelling to form a vibrant experience of artistic practice in North Carolina.

Artists include Senora Lynch (Haliwa-Saponi), Karina McMillan (Lumbee), Harlen Chavis (Lumbee), Aaron Baumgardner (Catawba),Coda Cavalier (Occaneechi Band of the Saponi Nation), Amy Postoak (Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians)& Johnny Postoak (Muscogee Creek)of Three Sisters Designs, Rhiannon “Skye” Tafoya (Eastern Band of Cherokee & Santa Clara Pueblo), Joshua Adams (Eastern Band of Cherokee), Idalis Dial (Coharie), Tim Locklear (Lumbee), NC State students Ashtyn Thomas (Lumbee) and Victoria Wilson (Haliwa-Saponi), Gwen Locklear (Lumbee) and Alexandra Williams portrait photographs of Powwows at Dix Park. Together, these artists explore heritage, craft, and storytelling as a living continuum of creativity, connecting ancestral knowledge with contemporary expression.

title: Through Our Eyes, In Our Hands: Prioritizing Indigenous Knowledge in Museums
description:
Through Our Eyes, In Our Hands: Prioritizing Indigenous Knowledge in Museums will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until June 27, 2026. This exhibition foregrounds Native perspectives on the stewardship of cultural belongings and the history and future of repatriation. This exhibition transforms the museum into a site of learning, self-examination, and responsibility.

Visitors are guided through the intertwined histories of museum collecting, cultural consultation, and the journey to repatriation. Archival materials, personal accounts, and community-based narratives offer insight into the significance of the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (NAGPRA) and the ongoing work beyond its legal requirements. Rather than presenting repatriation as a transactional process, this exhibition emphasizes its cultural, spiritual, emotional, and relational dimensions—its power to restore connections and honor ancestors and communities.

title: Durham Social Hack Night
description:
Triangle Developers
Hey tech folks, come out and hang at Hi-Wire starting at 6pm! Hack Night is meant to be a social evening for folks in tech. It's less about networking and more about community.

**Look for the Hack Night tabletop sign** and nerds wearing name tags to find us. If the weather is nice, we'll probably be outside.

Help folks feel welcome by using the **"Pac Man Rule"** \- when standing with a group of people \(usually in a circle\)\, leave some space open so that another person can easily join\.

See our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/TriangleDevsSlack/policies/blob/master/code-of-conduct.md). To summarize: be nice or leave. No tolerance for harassment or oppression. In addition, since alcohol is present at these events, please be mindful of your consumption and respect other people's choices on whether or not to consume.

**FAQs**
*Do folks hack at Hack Night? Should I bring my computer?*
This is more of a night for hackers than an actual hack night. You're welcome to bring a laptop, but most people will only be socializing.

*What are the beverage options? Are there any non-alcoholic drinks?*
Hi-Wire Brewing offers many types of beers including a few non-alcoholic options plus wine and some liquor. They usually have a happy hour special on the first few beers on the menu. In the same complex are Cugino Forno which has additional drink options, and Two Roosters which has excellent ice cream.

*Are there any drink specials?*
If Hack Night is on a Tuesday, Hi-Wire usually has $5 pints for their flagship beers. Look for the list at the counter.

*Do people eat snacks/dinner during the meetup?*
Sometimes folks will order a pizza or salad from Cugino Forno. I sometimes grab an ice cream from Two Roosters across the way. Most people eat before or after but it's no big deal - whatever you prefer and are most comfortable with.

*How can I connect with the developer community?*
Go to [triangledevelopers.com](https://triangledevelopers.com/) to find the Discord and Slack info.

How to join:
Please join our virtual welcome session with this link

Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage. 

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country. 

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare. 

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

How to prepare:
We are excited to see you soon!

P.S. This is a call for young people from 13-25 years old who are interested in getting engaged with the Team ENOUGH program. If you are over the age of 25 please sign up for the Brady Welcome Session at https://www.mobilize.us/brady/event/274016/

location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

title: Webinar: 7(a) Manufacturers’ Access to Revolving Credit Loans
description:
Join NC State Industry Expansion Solutions for a webinar that will focus on the Small Business Administration's (SBA) new 7(a) Manufacturers’ Access to Revolving Credit (MARC) Loans.

MARC is SBA’s first-ever loan program dedicated to supporting America’s small manufacturers, which make up 98% of all U.S. manufacturers. The program will offer working capital for small businesses engaged in manufacturing and is specifically designed to provide maximum flexibility and minimal red tape.

MARC complements the SBA’s core 7(a) and 504 loan programs, providing a flexible new line of credit to manufacturers and lenders. MARC loans can be used in combination with SBA and conventional commercial loans, making it a potent new tool in support of SBA's effort to reshore American industrial dominance.

title: Music at the Gregg With Mountain Walrus and Brittany Stephenson
location: Gregg Museum of Art & Design, Front Lawn
description:
Headlining the Gregg Museum’s Music at the Lawn concert will be Mountain Walrus, a group that serves up a unique brand of southern funk from the mountains of Southwest Virginia. Led by Foster Burton’s soulful songwriting, Mountain Walrus draws on elements of New Orleans funk and southern rock to create a sound that’s right at home in Appalachia. The band is quickly growing a fan base across the Southeast thanks to their dynamic live shows and appearances at festivals, such as FloydFest, Rooster Walk, the Mountain Music Festival and Floyd Yoga Jam. Burton is backed by Mason Jennelle on drums, Ben Hite on keys, Ryan Ratliff on saxophone and multi-instrumentalist Brach Rauchle. The band just released their new album, Less Is More, and has more music coming very soon.

Opening for Mountain Walrus will be Brittany Stephenson, a Dallas-based vocalist and multimedia artist blending folk storytelling with contemporary themes. Raised in a West Texas musical family, she performed extensively as a vocalist for The Coverlets at the Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, as well as the Smithsonian and the Metropolitan Museum. Now she creates performance art pieces that witness the weight and electricity of being human.

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

Te invitamos a participar en nuestro Taller de Salud Mental este miercoles 29 de Octubre a las 5:30 Hora del Pacifico, impartido por la **Dra. Sandra Martínez**, psicóloga y psicoterapeuta con más de 20 años de experiencia brindando apoyo emocional con un enfoque empático, profesional y humano. Taller de Salud Mental, 

**Este evento es gratuito y lo único que se necesita para entrar es tener una cuenta de Zoom. **

Este espacio está diseñado especialmente para la comunidad latina en EE. UU., con el propósito de ofrecer recursos prácticos y estrategias útiles para mejorar nuestra calidad de vida y afrontar con fortaleza estos tiempos de cambio e incertidumbre.

Durante el taller, hablaremos sobre temas esenciales como:

 - Bienestar emocional: la importancia de cuidar nuestra salud mental.

 - Manejo del estrés, miedo y ansiedad: herramientas y técnicas para recuperar el equilibrio.

 - Creación de espacios seguros: cómo cultivar la salud desde nosotros mismos.

 - Acompañamiento a nuestros hijos y comunidad: cómo, como madres y líderes, podemos apoyar, resistir y manejar el miedo.

 - Educación y apoyo en crisis: cómo acompañar de manera efectiva a quienes están pasando por momentos difíciles.

Además, contaremos con una sesión de preguntas y respuestas con la Dra. Sandra Martínez, donde podrás resolver tus dudas y compartir tus experiencias.

title: Mobilization Mondays: Chapel Hill (mornings)
location: East Franklin Street & South Elliott Road, Chapel Hill, NC, 27514
description:
Please join Engaged Defenders for Democracy on Mondays from 7:30-9 at the corner of Franklin St & Elliott Rd in Chapel Hill for a weekly, peaceful, nonpartisan protest and call to action. Free parking at the Church of Reconciliation, 110 N Elliott Rd.

Across the political spectrum, Americans are disillusioned by leaders who put power over people. We gather to build community, spark hope, and inspire action.

Bring a friend. Bring a sign. Speak up for immigrant rights, free speech, healthcare, social security, the environment, the Constitution and the rule of law, reproductive freedom, job and funding cuts, and the many, many other issues close to our hearts. Bonus points for signs that encourage others to move beyond honking and help turn awareness into action.  We often hand out fliers to stopped cars & pedestrians with information about relevant actions folks can take to support their community and defend democracy. We also have a Signal chat for regular attenders. If you are interested in either of these opportunities, ask around for Wendy.

This will be a POSITIVE and nonviolent demonstration. We are here to protect our democracy. We are standing up for what we believe in. We want to inspire people to join us and grow our movement!

Please bring positive signs supporting the movement and resisting what is happening in our country!

Please no mocking signs, no swastikas

We are excited to see you there and stand together for our country!

See you every Monday afternoon engaging drivers in Chapel Hill!

title: A Creek in Carolina: Artworks by Bobby C. Martin
description: A Creek in Carolina : Artworks by Bobby C. Martin will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. Nationally recognized artist Bobby C. Martin (Muscogee Creek) presents a solo exhibition tracing the pathways connecting ancestral Mvskoke homelands to Indian Territory. Drawing from family photographs and archival materials, Martin weaves encaustic, collage, maps, hymns, and personal imagery to reframe histories of forced removal as stories of resilience, survival, and continuity—inviting viewers to reflect on their own family histories and the enduring presence of Mvskoke people.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

title: Stories Told by Breath: Native American Voices in North Carolina
description:
Stories Told by Breath will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. This exhibition celebrates the creativity, memory, and cultural continuity of Native American artists connected to North Carolina. 

The exhibition brings together a rich range of media—clay, beadwork, textiles, printmaking, regalia, sculpture, and multimedia—woven with storytelling to form a vibrant experience of artistic practice in North Carolina.

Artists include Senora Lynch (Haliwa-Saponi), Karina McMillan (Lumbee), Harlen Chavis (Lumbee), Aaron Baumgardner (Catawba),Coda Cavalier (Occaneechi Band of the Saponi Nation), Amy Postoak (Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians)& Johnny Postoak (Muscogee Creek)of Three Sisters Designs, Rhiannon “Skye” Tafoya (Eastern Band of Cherokee & Santa Clara Pueblo), Joshua Adams (Eastern Band of Cherokee), Idalis Dial (Coharie), Tim Locklear (Lumbee), NC State students Ashtyn Thomas (Lumbee) and Victoria Wilson (Haliwa-Saponi), Gwen Locklear (Lumbee) and Alexandra Williams portrait photographs of Powwows at Dix Park. Together, these artists explore heritage, craft, and storytelling as a living continuum of creativity, connecting ancestral knowledge with contemporary expression.

title: Through Our Eyes, In Our Hands: Prioritizing Indigenous Knowledge in Museums
description:
Through Our Eyes, In Our Hands: Prioritizing Indigenous Knowledge in Museums will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until June 27, 2026. This exhibition foregrounds Native perspectives on the stewardship of cultural belongings and the history and future of repatriation. This exhibition transforms the museum into a site of learning, self-examination, and responsibility.

Visitors are guided through the intertwined histories of museum collecting, cultural consultation, and the journey to repatriation. Archival materials, personal accounts, and community-based narratives offer insight into the significance of the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (NAGPRA) and the ongoing work beyond its legal requirements. Rather than presenting repatriation as a transactional process, this exhibition emphasizes its cultural, spiritual, emotional, and relational dimensions—its power to restore connections and honor ancestors and communities.

title: Scaling AI: Designing Systems Built to Grow
description:
Data Science Raleigh
The path from prototype to production-grade AI isn’t linear—it’s architectural. As use cases grow more complex and expectations rise, so do the demands on your underlying systems. Scaling AI effectively means designing for modularity, reliability, observability, and performance from day one.

In this webinar, we’ll dig into the technical patterns that support AI at scale. From model deployment strategies and orchestration layers to real-time data pipelines and monitoring practices, we’ll explore how to architect AI systems that don’t buckle under growth—but get better with it.

**What You'll Learn:**

1️⃣ **Scalable Foundations:** Core components of an AI architecture that supports increasing complexity without sacrificing speed or reliability.

2️⃣ **Modular Design:** How to build workflows and services that are loosely coupled, easily governed, and ready for cross-functional collaboration.

3️⃣ **Observability in Practice:** Techniques for monitoring model behavior, tracking drift, and ensuring end-to-end visibility across the stack.

4️⃣ **Speed Without Sacrifice:** Strategies to maintain low-latency inference and fast iteration cycles—even as systems scale.

How to join:
Please join our virtual welcome session with this link

Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage. 

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country. 

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare. 

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

How to prepare:
We are excited to see you soon!

P.S. This is a call for young people from 13-25 years old who are interested in getting engaged with the Team ENOUGH program. If you are over the age of 25 please sign up for the Brady Welcome Session at https://www.mobilize.us/brady/event/274016/

The onslaught of news, the chaos coming out of the White House – it’s all meant to overwhelm us. It’s a deliberate strategy to sow confusion and make us believe we are powerless to fight back.

location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

location: Bridges will vary across the Triangle, Durham, NC, 27705
description: Come join Engaged Defenders for Democracy as we partner with the Overpass Coalition to have a Unified Bridge Brigade that covers bridges in the Triangle and beyond on the third Saturday of the month. We will have protectors on multiple bridges to show that we are not going away, we are not backing down, and we support our neighbors and workers. We also are uniting all of us over billionaires. We will have message about peace, unity, and defending our Constitution. We will host a Visibility Brigade event where drivers see our protectors and signs as they drive under overpasses in Durham, Raleigh, Cary, Pittsboro, and Chapel Hill. (we are coordinating with 10 other states). Please use the SignUp Genius to sign up for the bridge you will attend: https://www.signupgenius.com/go/10C0549A5AA23A1F8C43-61318184-cultivating#/ Even in cooler temperatures, sunburn and dehydration can be a problem. Please bring water, snacks, sun screen, a hat, sunglasses, and clothing suitable for the weather. The bridges get very breezy. You can learn details by visiting our website. https://durhamresistancehub.com/btfsite We will ask people to bring American flags and smaller signs if they have cars and pedestrians on the bridge. Please also bring Rainbow flags, Mexican flags, and Palestine flags. Please tell your friends to come. People loved driving under bridge after bridge seeing our protectors up there sharing a unified message. Please be part of this next coordinated event! Please join our Substack: https://substack.com/profile/115484101-engaged-defenders-4-democracy For more ED4D Mobilize Events: https://www.mobilize.us/engagedefendersfordemocracy/ Have accessibility questions? title: 18th Century Law and Order in the Historical Park
description: How did North Carolinians keep crime down and conduct legal matters in the backcountry? John Haley was a tax collector and sheriff - what was work like? Join our costumed interpreters as they talk about how 18th century society was policed and how laws were kept. FREE. All ages welcome. Drop-in.

title: Ballot Boxes & Cartridge Boxes
description:
"A man's rights rest in three boxes. The ballot box, jury box and the cartridge box. Let no man be kept from the ballot box because of his color. Let no woman be kept from the ballot box..." -Frederick Douglass, November 15th, 1867.


Join us in June for an exploration of voting rights in North Carolina and a deeper examination of the relationship between violence and political participation.

title: Battle of Ramsour's Mill
description:
The Battle of Ramsour’s Mill Living History Weekend commemorates the June 20, 1780 Battle of Ramsour’s Mill, when Whigs met Tories on a hillside just outside the little town of Lincolnton.

In 2026, the commemoration will take place the weekend of June 20 & 21 near Battleground Elementary School.

In between, hearth cooking demonstrations by the Lincoln County Hearth Cooks, reenactments and weapons demonstrations, a militia encampment, speakers and storytellers, heritage demonstrations, battleground tours, and period crafts. All activities are free.

Schedule is subject to change. Reenactors and demonstrators welcome! Reenactors who wish to participate should contact Lisa Pupkiewicz at lpupkie@gmail.com; suttlers should contact Beverly Moore at bkingnccp@gmail.com

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

Photo by J. Hill: 10-inch mortar demonstration during Labor Day Weekend Cannon Day at Ft. Macon State Park.

description:

This will include a blank firing demonstration of the weapon.
Meet in the fort parade ground.

title: Discover Tryon Palace: Outlander
location: Tryon Palace Historic Sites and Gardens
description:
Step into Tryon Palace and explore Diana Gabaldon’s award-winning Outlander series. Learn about the lives of the fictional Jamie and Claire Fraser, their family and friends, and interactions with historical figures and events in the tumultuous period of the American Revolution.

Tour covers storylines from Outlander books 4 – 8 and the Starz Outlander seasons 4 – 8. (For those not current on the books or show, there will be spoilers for these books and seasons.)

Tour begins at 301 George Street, across from the Tryon Palace Main Gates. Ticket holders should check in at the Waystation ticketing desk no later than 3:30 p.m.

title: Mobilization Mondays: Chapel Hill (mornings)
location: East Franklin Street & South Elliott Road, Chapel Hill, NC, 27514
description:
Please join Engaged Defenders for Democracy on Mondays from 7:30-9 at the corner of Franklin St & Elliott Rd in Chapel Hill for a weekly, peaceful, nonpartisan protest and call to action. Free parking at the Church of Reconciliation, 110 N Elliott Rd.

Across the political spectrum, Americans are disillusioned by leaders who put power over people. We gather to build community, spark hope, and inspire action.

Bring a friend. Bring a sign. Speak up for immigrant rights, free speech, healthcare, social security, the environment, the Constitution and the rule of law, reproductive freedom, job and funding cuts, and the many, many other issues close to our hearts. Bonus points for signs that encourage others to move beyond honking and help turn awareness into action.  We often hand out fliers to stopped cars & pedestrians with information about relevant actions folks can take to support their community and defend democracy. We also have a Signal chat for regular attenders. If you are interested in either of these opportunities, ask around for Wendy.

This will be a POSITIVE and nonviolent demonstration. We are here to protect our democracy. We are standing up for what we believe in. We want to inspire people to join us and grow our movement!

Please bring positive signs supporting the movement and resisting what is happening in our country!

Please no mocking signs, no swastikas

We are excited to see you there and stand together for our country!

See you every Monday afternoon engaging drivers in Chapel Hill!

Please join our Substack: https://substack.com/profile/115484101-engaged-defenders-4-democracy

For more ED4D Mobilize Events: https://www.mobilize.us/engagedefendersfordemocracy/

description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. title: A Creek in Carolina: Artworks by Bobby C. Martin
description: A Creek in Carolina : Artworks by Bobby C. Martin will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. Nationally recognized artist Bobby C. Martin (Muscogee Creek) presents a solo exhibition tracing the pathways connecting ancestral Mvskoke homelands to Indian Territory. Drawing from family photographs and archival materials, Martin weaves encaustic, collage, maps, hymns, and personal imagery to reframe histories of forced removal as stories of resilience, survival, and continuity—inviting viewers to reflect on their own family histories and the enduring presence of Mvskoke people.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

title: Stories Told by Breath: Native American Voices in North Carolina
description:
Stories Told by Breath will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. This exhibition celebrates the creativity, memory, and cultural continuity of Native American artists connected to North Carolina. 

The exhibition brings together a rich range of media—clay, beadwork, textiles, printmaking, regalia, sculpture, and multimedia—woven with storytelling to form a vibrant experience of artistic practice in North Carolina.

Artists include Senora Lynch (Haliwa-Saponi), Karina McMillan (Lumbee), Harlen Chavis (Lumbee), Aaron Baumgardner (Catawba),Coda Cavalier (Occaneechi Band of the Saponi Nation), Amy Postoak (Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians)& Johnny Postoak (Muscogee Creek)of Three Sisters Designs, Rhiannon “Skye” Tafoya (Eastern Band of Cherokee & Santa Clara Pueblo), Joshua Adams (Eastern Band of Cherokee), Idalis Dial (Coharie), Tim Locklear (Lumbee), NC State students Ashtyn Thomas (Lumbee) and Victoria Wilson (Haliwa-Saponi), Gwen Locklear (Lumbee) and Alexandra Williams portrait photographs of Powwows at Dix Park. Together, these artists explore heritage, craft, and storytelling as a living continuum of creativity, connecting ancestral knowledge with contemporary expression.

title: Through Our Eyes, In Our Hands: Prioritizing Indigenous Knowledge in Museums
description:
Through Our Eyes, In Our Hands: Prioritizing Indigenous Knowledge in Museums will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until June 27, 2026. This exhibition foregrounds Native perspectives on the stewardship of cultural belongings and the history and future of repatriation. This exhibition transforms the museum into a site of learning, self-examination, and responsibility.

Visitors are guided through the intertwined histories of museum collecting, cultural consultation, and the journey to repatriation. Archival materials, personal accounts, and community-based narratives offer insight into the significance of the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act (NAGPRA) and the ongoing work beyond its legal requirements. Rather than presenting repatriation as a transactional process, this exhibition emphasizes its cultural, spiritual, emotional, and relational dimensions—its power to restore connections and honor ancestors and communities.

description:
Join the Chatham Community Library for this Goldston America 250 Film Series, hosted every fourth Tuesday, January-December 2026, 4pm-6pm. The Goldston Library will screen the following documentaries and films:

Tue, Jan 27, 4pm-6pm The Congress, Ken Burns.
Tue, Feb 24, 4pm-6pm Becoming Frederick Douglass, Stanley Nelson and Nicole London.
Tue, Mar 24, 4pm-6pm Rachel Carson: The Woman Who Launched the Modern Environmental Movement, Michelle Ferrari.
Tue, Apr 28, 4pm-6pm Thomas Jefferson: A View from the Mountain, Martin Doblmeier.
Tue, May 26, 4pm-6pm The Address, Ken Burns.
Tue, Jun 23, 4pm-6pm The Brooklyn Bridge, Ken Burns.
Tue, Jul 28, 4pm-6pm The Statue of Liberty, Ken Burns.
Tue, Aug 25, 4pm-6pm American Coup: Wilmington 1898, Yoruba Richen and Brad Lichtenstein.
Tue, Sep 22, 4pm-6pm How it Feels to be Free, Yoruba Richen.
Tue, Oct 27, 4pm-6pm 80 Years Later, Celine Parreñas Shimizu.
Tue, Nov 24, 4pm-6pm Gather, Sanjay Rawal.
Tue, Dec 22, 4pm-6pm Women of World War II: The Untold Stories, Eli Brown.

This FREE, family-friendly event is open to the public. No registration is required. The event will take place indoors in the Goldston Library. The Goldston Library is ADA-compliant, including wheelchair-accessible parking, entrances, seating, common spaces, walkways, and restrooms. Free parking is available outside the library. Pets are not allowed - please leave your furry friends at home.

This event is part of our Chatham Celebrates America 250 initiative. See more America 250 events.

How to join:
Please join our virtual welcome session with this link

Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage. 

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country. 

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare. 

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

How to prepare:
We are excited to see you soon!

P.S. This is a call for young people from 13-25 years old who are interested in getting engaged with the Team ENOUGH program. If you are over the age of 25 please sign up for the Brady Welcome Session at https://www.mobilize.us/brady/event/274016/

location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

title: Tours of the Moravian Archives Vault -- America 250 Theme
description:
Join us for a tour of the Moravian Archives Vault featuring the collection materials from the Revolutionary War and early American History!

Guests will walk through the Archives Vault which contains millions of records from the settlement of the Moravians here in North Carolina in the 1750s on. Highlighted items will include correspondence from George Washington, the Fourth of July Proclamation, maps, congressional records and much, much more!

Learn about Moravian History and the creation of our nation while seeing how such collection materials are preserved for our posterity!

title: NC 4th of July Festival
description:
2026 NC 4th of July Festival: Celebrating 250 Years of Independence
June 28 – July 4, 2026 | Southport, North Carolina

Join us in historic Southport for one of North Carolina’s most beloved traditions, the NC 4th of July Festival. In 2026, the celebration takes on even greater meaning as we honor the 250th anniversary of American independence, part of the nationwide America250 Semiquincentennial.

For over two centuries, communities across North Carolina have gathered to mark our nation’s birthday. This year, from June 28 through July 4, the NC 4th of July Festival will bring together visitors for a week of parades, concerts, arts and crafts, family activities, and patriotic ceremonies, all infused with the spirit of America’s 250th birthday.

Festival Highlights

Grand Parade featuring floats, marching bands, and community groups decked out in patriotic spirit

Live Music & Entertainment on multiple stages, showcasing diverse voices and talents from across the region

Fireworks Over the Water — a breathtaking tradition made even more meaningful in this Semiquincentennial year

Arts, Crafts & Food Vendors with local flavors and handmade treasures

Family Activities, including games, educational exhibits, and history-themed programming inspired by America250

description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. title: Chatham Celebrates America 250: Cumulative Celebration
description:
July 4, 2026, marks 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Join Chatham Celebrates America 250 in recognizing the Semiquincentennial during our

July 4, 2026, marks 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Join Chatham Celebrates America 250 in recognizing the Semiquincentennial during our Cumulative Celebration on Sat, Jun 27, 2026, 10am-2pm. Admission is free. Together, we’ll remember the events that have shaped our history, reflect on the present, and envision a promising future for the next generation.

Festivities will include live music and performances, food trucks, vendors, displays and demonstrations, activities for children, and much more. If you are interested in participating, volunteering, or getting involved in other ways, please contact Lindsay Ray at lindsay.ray@chathamcountync.gov or 919.545.8302.

This free, family-friendly event takes place indoors at the Chatham County Agriculture & Conference Center (CCACC). Shuttle services will be provided by Chatham Transit. CCACC is an ADA-compliant space, featuring wheelchair-accessible parking, entrances, shared spaces, and walkways. Since most of the festivities will take place indoors, this event will not be pet-friendly. Please leave your furry friends at home. Service animals are welcome.

See more America 250 events. Learn more on the Chatham Celebrates America 250 Microsite. See more events at the Chatham County Agriculture & Conference Center.

America 250 NC is North Carolina's commemoration planning organization responsible for leading the initiative and collaborating with various local, state, and federal partners.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

title: NC 4th of July Festival
description:
2026 NC 4th of July Festival: Celebrating 250 Years of Independence
June 28 – July 4, 2026 | Southport, North Carolina

Join us in historic Southport for one of North Carolina’s most beloved traditions, the NC 4th of July Festival. In 2026, the celebration takes on even greater meaning as we honor the 250th anniversary of American independence, part of the nationwide America250 Semiquincentennial.

For over two centuries, communities across North Carolina have gathered to mark our nation’s birthday. This year, from June 28 through July 4, the NC 4th of July Festival will bring together visitors for a week of parades, concerts, arts and crafts, family activities, and patriotic ceremonies, all infused with the spirit of America’s 250th birthday.

Festival Highlights

Grand Parade featuring floats, marching bands, and community groups decked out in patriotic spirit

Live Music & Entertainment on multiple stages, showcasing diverse voices and talents from across the region

Fireworks Over the Water — a breathtaking tradition made even more meaningful in this Semiquincentennial year

Arts, Crafts & Food Vendors with local flavors and handmade treasures

Family Activities, including games, educational exhibits, and history-themed programming inspired by America250

Commemorative Programs highlighting North Carolina’s role in the American story, from 1776 to today

America250 Connection

As part of the America250 NC initiative, this year’s festival will not only celebrate our nation’s founding ideals — liberty, democracy, and unity — but also spotlight the diverse stories that make up our shared history. Through special exhibits, performances, and community programs, festival-goers will be invited to reflect on the past, celebrate the present, and imagine the next 250 years together.

Why 2026 is Special

This year’s festival isn’t just a tradition; it’s part of a once-in-a-generation national celebration. By joining us in Southport, you’ll be part of history, experiencing one of the largest and most vibrant Independence Day events in North Carolina during America’s Semiquincentennial.

description:

title: A Creek in Carolina: Artworks by Bobby C. Martin
description: A Creek in Carolina : Artworks by Bobby C. Martin will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. Nationally recognized artist Bobby C. Martin (Muscogee Creek) presents a solo exhibition tracing the pathways connecting ancestral Mvskoke homelands to Indian Territory. Drawing from family photographs and archival materials, Martin weaves encaustic, collage, maps, hymns, and personal imagery to reframe histories of forced removal as stories of resilience, survival, and continuity—inviting viewers to reflect on their own family histories and the enduring presence of Mvskoke people.

title: Staying Alive
location: North Carolina Museum of Natural Sciences
description:
March 14 – August 23, 2026

In the ultimate battle for survival, every animal has a plan.

Explore the striking ways nature fights back in “Staying Alive,” featuring 17 live animals from around the world with unbelievable self-defense strategies. Come face to face with trippy toads, armored armadillos, a two-toed sloth and more.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.

title: Stories Told by Breath: Native American Voices in North Carolina
description:
Stories Told by Breath will be on display at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design Tuesday-Saturday until September 26, 2026. This exhibition celebrates the creativity, memory, and cultural continuity of Native American artists connected to North Carolina. 

The exhibition brings together a rich range of media—clay, beadwork, textiles, printmaking, regalia, sculpture, and multimedia—woven with storytelling to form a vibrant experience of artistic practice in North Carolina.

Artists include Senora Lynch (Haliwa-Saponi), Karina McMillan (Lumbee), Harlen Chavis (Lumbee), Aaron Baumgardner (Catawba),Coda Cavalier (Occaneechi Band of the Saponi Nation), Amy Postoak (Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians)& Johnny Postoak (Muscogee Creek)of Three Sisters Designs, Rhiannon “Skye” Tafoya (Eastern Band of Cherokee & Santa Clara Pueblo), Joshua Adams (Eastern Band of Cherokee), Idalis Dial (Coharie), Tim Locklear (Lumbee), NC State students Ashtyn Thomas (Lumbee) and Victoria Wilson (Haliwa-Saponi), Gwen Locklear (Lumbee) and Alexandra Williams portrait photographs of Powwows at Dix Park. Together, these artists explore heritage, craft, and storytelling as a living continuum of creativity, connecting ancestral knowledge with contemporary expression.

Please join our virtual welcome session with this link

Are you a young person between 13 and 25 years old who is interested in taking action around preventing gun violence? Join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session to learn more about the different ways you can engage. 

Team ENOUGH is a youth-led program whose mission is to educate young voices about gun violence and mobilize them to take meaningful action against it. Supported by Brady United, we harness the expertise and experience of today’s youth to advance our intersectional work across the country. 

Led by an Executive Council, comprised of students just like us, we believe that diversity is a strength, and that only when everyone has a seat at the table can we build an effective movement to prevent all gun violence in all communities.

For us, preventing gun violence not only requires regulating access to firearms but also addressing how systemic racism and environmental factors cause this form of bloodshed to run especially rampant in communities of color. You cannot talk about gun violence without talking about police brutality, white supremacy, the broken criminal justice system, poverty, homophobia, access to affordable housing, or the often barriers separating disadvantaged populations from physical and mental healthcare. 

So if you share this belief, join us for our Team ENOUGH welcome session and become part of the movement to end gun violence in our lifetime.

title: NC 4th of July Festival
description:
2026 NC 4th of July Festival: Celebrating 250 Years of Independence
June 28 – July 4, 2026 | Southport, North Carolina

Join us in historic Southport for one of North Carolina’s most beloved traditions, the NC 4th of July Festival. In 2026, the celebration takes on even greater meaning as we honor the 250th anniversary of American independence, part of the nationwide America250 Semiquincentennial.

For over two centuries, communities across North Carolina have gathered to mark our nation’s birthday. This year, from June 28 through July 4, the NC 4th of July Festival will bring together visitors for a week of parades, concerts, arts and crafts, family activities, and patriotic ceremonies, all infused with the spirit of America’s 250th birthday.

Festival Highlights

Grand Parade featuring floats, marching bands, and community groups decked out in patriotic spirit

Live Music & Entertainment on multiple stages, showcasing diverse voices and talents from across the region

Fireworks Over the Water — a breathtaking tradition made even more meaningful in this Semiquincentennial year

Arts, Crafts & Food Vendors with local flavors and handmade treasures

Family Activities, including games, educational exhibits, and history-themed programming inspired by America250

Commemorative Programs highlighting North Carolina’s role in the American story, from 1776 to today

America250 Connection

As part of the America250 NC initiative, this year’s festival will not only celebrate our nation’s founding ideals — liberty, democracy, and unity — but also spotlight the diverse stories that make up our shared history. Through special exhibits, performances, and community programs, festival-goers will be invited to reflect on the past, celebrate the present, and imagine the next 250 years together.

Why 2026 is Special

This year’s festival isn’t just a tradition; it’s part of a once-in-a-generation national celebration. By joining us in Southport, you’ll be part of history, experiencing one of the largest and most vibrant Independence Day events in North Carolina during America’s Semiquincentennial.

title: Killer Dunes
description:
Join Us for the Jockey's Ridge Challenge!

Get ready for an exhilarating experience at Jockey's Ridge State Park as we proudly host the Jockey's Ridge Challenge! This exciting event invites participants to run, walk, or overcome a thrilling 2-mile course on the tallest natural sand dune system in the eastern United States.

 

Whether you're a seasoned runner seeking a "unique" challenge or a walker looking to enjoy the stunning views, this event is perfect for everyone! While the course promises a competitive atmosphere, it also welcomes those who want to take in the breathtaking scenery at a more leisurely pace.

 

By participating, you'll be contributing to a worthy cause. Proceeds from the Jockey's Ridge Challenge will benefit Friends of Jockey's Ridge, a local non-profit organization dedicated to supporting, preserving, and enhancing Jockey's Ridge State Park for future generations!

 

To honor our brave service members, they will be offering a $5 discount for Active US Military and Veterans. Join us for a day of fun, fitness, and community spirit at Jockey's Ridge!

General Pricing includes:

2 Mile Dunes Race (Age 17 & Up) $55.00

2 Mile Dunes Race (Age 10-16) $30.00

title: NC 4th of July Festival
description:
2026 NC 4th of July Festival: Celebrating 250 Years of Independence
June 28 – July 4, 2026 | Southport, North Carolina

Join us in historic Southport for one of North Carolina’s most beloved traditions, the NC 4th of July Festival. In 2026, the celebration takes on even greater meaning as we honor the 250th anniversary of American independence, part of the nationwide America250 Semiquincentennial.

For over two centuries, communities across North Carolina have gathered to mark our nation’s birthday. This year, from June 28 through July 4, the NC 4th of July Festival will bring together visitors for a week of parades, concerts, arts and crafts, family activities, and patriotic ceremonies, all infused with the spirit of America’s 250th birthday.

Festival Highlights

Grand Parade featuring floats, marching bands, and community groups decked out in patriotic spirit

Live Music & Entertainment on multiple stages, showcasing diverse voices and talents from across the region

Fireworks Over the Water — a breathtaking tradition made even more meaningful in this Semiquincentennial year

Arts, Crafts & Food Vendors with local flavors and handmade treasures

Family Activities, including games, educational exhibits, and history-themed programming inspired by America250

Commemorative Programs highlighting North Carolina’s role in the American story, from 1776 to today

America250 Connection

As part of the America250 NC initiative, this year’s festival will not only celebrate our nation’s founding ideals — liberty, democracy, and unity — but also spotlight the diverse stories that make up our shared history. Through special exhibits, performances, and community programs, festival-goers will be invited to reflect on the past, celebrate the present, and imagine the next 250 years together.

Why 2026 is Special

This year’s festival isn’t just a tradition; it’s part of a once-in-a-generation national celebration. By joining us in Southport, you’ll be part of history, experiencing one of the largest and most vibrant Independence Day events in North Carolina during America’s Semiquincentennial.

title: Frederick Douglass Community Reading at Stagville
description:
Commemorate Independence Day with a reading of Frederick Douglass' powerful Fourth of July address, "What to the Slave is the Fourth of July" at Historic Stagville State Historic Site. 

This is a participatory community reading. Every year, 60 volunteers sign up to read passages from this famous abolitionist speech in front of the historic slave quarters at Horton Grove. You may sign up as a reader when you arrive. 

This year's reading will mark a special date for reflection and remembrance: the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence. Douglass delivered this powerful speech about freedom and injustice on July 5, 1852, at an Independence Day celebration in Rochester, New York. Douglass' speech remains one of the most famous abolitionist texts in United States history. The speech resonates today, inviting all to reflect on the United States' founding ideals and our shared history of slavery and freedom.

A PDF of the speech text will be available via Historic Stagville's website. We suggest you print or download your own copy to bring to follow along! Some copies will be available in person at the event.

Bring a chair or blanket to sit on the grounds. The event will be outdoors at the historic slave quarters at Horton Grove at 5925 Jock Road, Bahama, NC 27503. Attendees must walk less than one hundred yards over uneven grass or gravel to reach the reading site. Porta-potties will be available on site.

This free event lasts about 1 hour, with the option to view inside the original slave quarters or Great Barn at Horton Grove afterwards.

title: Independence Day Celebration at Old Salem
location: Old Salem Museums & Gardens, Old Salem Visitor Center and the Historic District
description:
Celebrate the Fourth of July at Old Salem!

Did you know the first official Fourth of July Celebration in North Carolina was held in Old Salem? In 1783, Governor Alexander Martin proclaimed July 4th a day of thanksgiving and peace, and Salem residents gathered for food, fellowship, and festivities. This year, we invite you to be part of that tradition.

Join us for a full day of music, history, and hands-on experiences as we welcome visitors of all ages to commemorate Independence Day at the site of North Carolina’s very first July 4th celebration.

Explore Old Salem Museums & Gardens—a historic site sharing the stories of Moravian, Black, and Indigenous peoples in the American South. Our museums, historic town, and gardens offer an immersive and memorable historical experience for all visitors.

Event Highlights

Revolutionary War–Era Music
Hear authentic period music and learn how troops used sound as a communication tool during the war. Enjoy worship pieces composed by Moravian musicians—just as Salem residents did in their weekly services.

Historic Demonstrations
• Fire Bucket Brigade – Discover how early firefighters managed emergencies before hand-pumped engines.
• Historic Firearms – Watch demonstrations of the types of firearms crafted and used in Salem.
• Frozen Treat Making – Visit the Vogler House to see how early Salem residents created one of America’s favorite sweet treats.

Declaration of Independence Readings
Join us throughout the day for readings of the Declaration of Independence in honor of the 250th anniversary of its signing.

Guided Tours
Meet our costumed interpreters and explore the Historic Town of Salem on a guided tour.

All activities are included with standard ticket admission. Reserve your spot today and celebrate the Fourth of July in historic style!

title: History on Display
location: Davie County Public Library, Martin-Wall History Room
description:
You are invited to explore the history of Davie County as the Semiquincentennial draws closer. There will be historical artifacts on display representing the county's history. This includes a portrait of Continental Army Colonel William R. Davie, the county's namesake. There's also a lot of information on Daniel Boone, who lived in Davie County for seven years. His parents are buried in Mocksville's Joppa Cemetery. Feel free to browse around the room and examine historical records and documents, including a list of those who served during the American Revolution. 

These artifacts and documents are located inside the Martin-Wall History Room within the Davie County Public Library in Mocksville. This room acts as the Davie County history museum. Paying a visit will allow you to explore the county's long and proud history while gaining a better understanding of the Semiquincentennial's significance. These artifacts will be on display from Monday, March 16, until at least Sunday, July 6.

Discover how these defenders deploy an amazing arsenal of high-fashion camouflage and mimicry, specialized armor and advanced chemical warfare – like stink bombs, caboose cannons and smoke screens – to hide in plain sight, stand their ground or even drop a limb and make a run for it. Enjoy live animal encounters, larger-than-life sculptures, 3D tactile experiences and interactive programs.

Perfect for families and animal enthusiasts of all ages. Offered in English & Spanish.
